translations.literal: Da Xiwu, Ruo Ganhui, Yi Feng, Liu Liang, Wang De, He Lianda, Han Guo, Cai You, Chang Shan, Xin Wei, She Dichang, Liang Chun, Liang Tai, Tian Hong
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu, Ruo Ganhui, Yi Feng, Liu Liang, Wang De, He Lianda, Han Guo, Cai You, Chang Shan, Xin Wei, She Dichang, Liang Chun, Liang Tai, and Tian Hong

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十三

translations.literal: Biographies number fifty-three
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 53

sentences.zh: 達奚武若干惠怡峰劉亮王德赫連達韓果蔡祐常善辛威厙狄昌梁椿梁台田弘子仁恭孫德懋

translations.literal: Da Xiwu, Ruo Ganhui, Yi Feng, Liu Liang, Wang De, He Lianda, Han Guo, Cai You, Chang Shan, Xin Wei, She Dichang, Liang Chun, Liang Tai, Tian Hong; son Ren Gong; grandson Demao
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu, Ruo Ganhui, Yi Feng, Liu Liang, Wang De, He Lianda, Han Guo, Cai You, Chang Shan, Xin Wei, She Dichang, Liang Chun, Liang Tai, Tian Hong; [son:] Ren Gong; [grandson:] Demao

sentences.zh: 達奚武，字成興，代人也。

translations.literal: Da Xiwu, style name Chengxing, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu, courtesy name Chengxing, was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 祖眷，父長，並為鎮將。

translations.literal: His grandfather Juan and his father Chang both were garrison generals.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Juan and his father Chang had both served as garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 武少倜儻好馳射，賀拔岳征關右，引為別將。

translations.literal: Wu in youth was bold and unrestrained and loved riding and shooting; when Heba Yue campaigned in Guanxi, he was brought in as a separate commander.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Wu was bold and free-spirited and loved horsemanship and archery. When Heba Yue campaigned in the Guanxi region, Wu was appointed a separate commander.

sentences.zh: 及岳為侯莫陳悅所害，武與趙貴收屍歸平涼，同翊載周文帝。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, Wu together with Zhao Gui recovered the corpse and returned to Pingliang, jointly supporting the carriage to install Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, Wu and Zhao Gui recovered the body and returned to Pingliang, where together they supported the carriage to install Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 從平悅，封須昌縣伯。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Yue, he was enfeoffed as Count of Xuchang county.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Yue, he was enfeoffed as Count of Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 大統初，自大丞相府中兵參軍出為東秦州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, from military adjutant in the Grand Chancellor's office he went out as Regional Inspector of Dongqin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Datong era, he was transferred from military adjutant in the Grand Chancellor's office to Regional Inspector of Dongqin.

sentences.zh: 齊神武與竇泰、高敖曹三道來侵，周文欲並兵擊泰，諸將多異議，唯武及蘇綽與周文意同，遂禽之。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu with Dou Tai and Gao Aocao came to invade on three routes; Emperor Wen of Zhou wished to concentrate troops to strike Tai; the generals mostly disagreed; only Wu and Su Chuo agreed with Emperor Wen, and they consequently captured him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan invaded along three routes with Dou Tai and Gao Aocao, Emperor Wen of Zhou wished to concentrate forces and strike Dou Tai. Most of the generals disagreed; only Wu and Su Chuo shared his view, and they consequently captured Tai.

sentences.zh: 周文進圖弘農，遣武從兩騎覘候。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen advanced to besiege Hongnong and dispatched Wu with two horsemen to reconnoiter.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen advanced to besiege Hongnong and sent Wu with two horsemen to scout.

sentences.zh: 武與其候奇遇，即交戰，斬六級，獲三人而反。

translations.literal: Wu unexpectedly encountered their scouts; they immediately joined battle; he cut off six heads, captured three men, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wu unexpectedly encountered enemy scouts and immediately joined battle. He cut off six heads, captured three men, and returned.

sentences.zh: 齊神武趣沙苑，周文復遣武覘之。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu hurried to Shaya; Emperor Wen again sent Wu to scout.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan hurried to Shaya, Emperor Wen again sent Wu to reconnoiter.

sentences.zh: 武從三騎，皆衣敵人衣，至暮，下馬潛聽其軍號，曆營若警夜者，有不如法者，往往撻之。

translations.literal: Wu followed with three horsemen, all wearing enemy clothing; by evening he dismounted and secretly listened to their army passwords; he went through the camps like a night watchman; whenever anyone was not according to regulation, he often beat them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu rode with three men, all dressed in enemy clothing. By evening he dismounted and secretly listened to their army passwords, passing through the camps like a night watchman; whenever anyone was out of line, he often beat them.

sentences.zh: 具知敵情以告，周文遂從破之。

translations.literal: Having fully learned the enemy situation he reported it; Emperor Wen thereupon followed and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Having learned the enemy situation in full, he reported it, and Emperor Wen thereupon broke and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 進爵高陽郡公。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to Duke of Gaoyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was advanced to Duke of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 四年，周文援洛陽，武為前鋒，與李弼破莫多婁貸文。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Emperor Wen came to the relief of Luoyang; Wu was vanguard and together with Li Bi defeated Mo Duolou Daiwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Emperor Wen came to the relief of Luoyang, Wu served as vanguard and together with Li Bi defeated Mo Duolou Daiwen.

sentences.zh: 又進至河橋，力戰，斬其司徒高敖曹。

translations.literal: Again advancing to Heqiao, he fought fiercely and beheaded their Minister of Works Gao Aocao.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing further to Heqiao, he fought fiercely and beheaded their Minister of Works, Gao Aocao.

sentences.zh: 再遷雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Again he was transferred to Regional Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to Regional Inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 復從戰芒山，時大軍不利，齊神武乘勝進軍至陝。

translations.literal: Again he followed into battle at Mangshan; at the time the great army was at a disadvantage; Qi Shenwu pressed his victory and advanced the army to Shan.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed into battle at Mangshan. At the time the main army was at a disadvantage, and Gao Huan pressed his victory and marched as far as Shan.

sentences.zh: 武禦之，乃退。

translations.literal: Wu resisted him, and he then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wu resisted him, and Gao Huan then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十七年，詔武經略漢川。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, an edict ordered Wu to conduct military operations in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, an edict ordered Wu to conduct military operations in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 梁梁州刺史宜豐侯蕭修固守南鄭。

translations.literal: Xiao Xiu, Marquis of Yifeng and Regional Inspector of Liangzhou for Liang, firmly defended Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xiu, Marquis of Yifeng and Liangzhou inspector for the Liang, held firm at Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 武圍之，修請服。

translations.literal: Wu besieged him; Xiu requested to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Wu besieged him, and Xiu requested to surrender.

sentences.zh: 會梁武陵王遣其將楊乾運等救修，修更不下。

translations.literal: Just then the Prince of Wuling of Liang sent his generals Yang Qianyun and others to rescue Xiu; Xiu again would not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Prince of Wuling of Liang sent his generals Yang Qianyun and others to rescue Xiu, and Xiu again refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 武擊走乾運，修乃降。

translations.literal: Wu struck and routed Qianyun; Xiu then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wu routed Qianyun, and Xiu then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 自斂門以北悉平。

translations.literal: From Shimen northward all was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Everything north of Shimen was entirely pacified.

sentences.zh: 明年，振旅還京師。

translations.literal: The next year he led the troops back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he led his troops back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲以武為柱國，武曰：「我作柱國，不應在元子孝前。」

translations.literal: At court it was proposed to make Wu a pillar of state; Wu said: "If I am made pillar of state, I ought not to rank ahead of Yuenzi Xiao."
translations.idiomatic: At court it was proposed to appoint Wu as Pillar of State. Wu said, "If I am made Pillar of State, I ought not to rank ahead of Yuenzi Xiao."

sentences.zh: 固辭。

translations.literal: He firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 以大將軍出鎮玉壁。

translations.literal: As Grand General he went out to garrison Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand General he went out to garrison Yubi.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，授柱國、大司寇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou acceded to the throne, he was appointed pillar of state and Grand Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou acceded to the throne, Wu was appointed Pillar of State and Grand Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 齊北豫州刺史司馬消難舉州來附，詔武與楊忠迎消難以歸。

translations.literal: Sima Xiaonan, Regional Inspector of Beiyu of Qi, raised the province and came over; an edict ordered Wu together with Yang Zhong to welcome Xiaonan back.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiaonan, Regional Inspector of Beiyu in Qi, raised the province and defected. An edict ordered Wu and Yang Zhong to welcome Xiaonan back.

sentences.zh: 武成實，轉大宗伯，進封鄭國公。

translations.literal: When Wu accomplished the mission, he was transferred to Grand Director of Ceremonies and advanced to Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu accomplished the mission, he was transferred to Grand Director of Ceremonies and advanced to Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 齊將斛律敦侵汾、絳，武禦之，敦退。

translations.literal: The Qi general Hulu Dun invaded Fen and Jiang; Wu resisted him; Dun withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi general Hulu Dun invaded Fen and Jiang. Wu resisted him, and Dun withdrew.

sentences.zh: 武築柏壁城，留開府權嚴、薛羽生守之。

translations.literal: Wu built Boibi city and left the opening-generals Quan Yan and Xue Yusheng to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu built Boibi city and left the opening-generals Quan Yan and Xue Yusheng to defend it.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，遷太保。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, he was transferred to Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoding, he was transferred to Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 其年，大軍東伐，隨公楊忠引突厥自北道，武以三萬騎自東道期會晉陽。

translations.literal: That year the great army marched east to attack; Duke of Sui Yang Zhong led the Turks by the northern route; Wu with thirty thousand cavalry by the eastern route arranged to meet at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: That year the main army marched east to attack. Duke of Sui Yang Zhong led the Turks by the northern route, while Wu with thirty thousand cavalry took the eastern route to rendezvous at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 武至平陽，後期不進，而忠已還，武尚未知。

translations.literal: Wu reached Pingyang but was late and did not advance; Zhong had already returned; Wu did not yet know.
translations.idiomatic: Wu reached Pingyang but was late and did not advance, while Zhong had already returned—Wu did not yet know this.

sentences.zh: 齊將斛律明月遣武書曰：「鴻鶴已翔於寥廓，羅者猶視於沮澤也。」

translations.literal: The Qi general Hulu Mingyue sent Wu a letter saying: "The swan has already soared in the vast sky; the fowler still gazes at the marsh."
translations.idiomatic: The Qi general Hulu Mingyue sent Wu a letter saying, "The swan has already soared into the vast sky, yet the fowler still gazes at the marsh."

sentences.zh: 武覽書，乃班師。

translations.literal: Wu read the letter and then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wu read the letter and then withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Regional Inspector of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Regional Inspector of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，從晉公護東伐。

translations.literal: The next year he followed Duke of Jin Hu on the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he followed Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu on the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 時尉遲迥圍洛陽，為敵所敗。

translations.literal: At the time Yu Chi Jiong was besieging Luoyang and was defeated by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuchi Jiong was besieging Luoyang and was defeated by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 武與齊王憲於芒山禦之。

translations.literal: Wu together with Prince of Qi Xian resisted at Mangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian resisted at Mangshan.

sentences.zh: 至夜，收軍。

translations.literal: At night they recalled the army.
translations.idiomatic: At night they recalled the army.

sentences.zh: 憲欲待明更戰。

translations.literal: Xian wished to wait until dawn and fight again.
translations.idiomatic: Xian wished to wait until dawn and fight again.

sentences.zh: 武曰：「洛陽軍散，人情駭動，不因夜速還，明日欲歸不得。」

translations.literal: Wu said: "The army at Luoyang has scattered; the people's hearts are shaken with alarm; if we do not quickly return by night, tomorrow we will not be able to go home."
translations.idiomatic: Wu said, "The army at Luoyang has scattered and the people's hearts are shaken with alarm. If we do not quickly return by night, tomorrow we will not be able to go home."

sentences.zh: 憲從之，遂全軍而返。

translations.literal: Xian followed his advice; they consequently returned with the whole army.
translations.idiomatic: Xian followed his advice, and they returned with the whole army intact.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，轉太傅。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe, he was transferred to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe, he was transferred to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 武微時，奢侈好華飾。

translations.literal: In his early years Wu was extravagant and fond of fine adornment.
translations.idiomatic: In his early years Wu was extravagant and fond of fine adornment.

sentences.zh: 及居重位，不持威儀，行常單馬，左右從一兩人而已，門外不施戟，恆晝掩一扉。

translations.literal: When he attained high rank, he did not maintain imposing ceremonial display; he usually traveled with a single horse and only one or two attendants at his side; outside his gate he did not set up halberds; by day he always kept only one leaf of the double door closed.
translations.idiomatic: After he attained high rank, he did not maintain imposing ceremonial display. He usually traveled with a single horse and only one or two attendants; outside his gate he did not set up halberds, and by day he always kept only one leaf of the double door closed.

sentences.zh: 或謂曰：「公位冠群後，何輕率若是？」

translations.literal: Someone said to him: "Your eminence stands above all the nobles—why are you so careless?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to him, "Your eminence stands above all the nobles—why are you so careless?"

sentences.zh: 武曰：「吾昔在布衣，豈望富貴！

translations.literal: Wu said: "In the past when I was a commoner, how could I have hoped for wealth and rank!
translations.idiomatic: Wu said, "In the past when I was a commoner, how could I have hoped for wealth and rank!

sentences.zh: 今日富貴，不可頓忘疇昔。

translations.literal: Now that I have wealth and rank, I cannot suddenly forget the past.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have wealth and rank, I cannot suddenly forget the past.

sentences.zh: 且天下未平，國恩未報，安可過事威容乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover the realm is not yet pacified and the grace of the state is not yet repaid—how can I indulge in excessive pomp and ceremony?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the realm is not yet pacified and the grace of the state is not yet repaid—how can I indulge in excessive pomp and ceremony?"

sentences.zh: 言者慚而退。

translations.literal: The speaker withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: The speaker withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 武之在同州，時旱，武帝敕武祀華嶽。

translations.literal: While Wu was at Tongzhou, there was drought; Emperor Wu ordered Wu to sacrifice to Mount Hua.
translations.idiomatic: While Wu was at Tongzhou, there was drought. Emperor Wu ordered Wu to offer sacrifice to Mount Hua.

sentences.zh: 嶽廟舊在山下，常所祈禱。

translations.literal: The peak temple had been at the foot of the mountain and was the usual place for prayer.
translations.idiomatic: The temple of the peak had long stood at the foot of the mountain and was the usual place for prayer.

sentences.zh: 武謂僚屬曰：「吾備位三公，不能燮理陰陽，不可同於眾人，在常祀所，必須登峰展誠，尋其聖奧。」

translations.literal: Wu said to his staff: "I hold one of the three highest offices yet cannot harmonize yin and yang—I cannot be the same as the multitude at the usual shrine; I must climb to the summit to display sincerity and seek the sacred mystery."
translations.idiomatic: Wu said to his staff, "I hold one of the three highest offices yet cannot harmonize yin and yang—I cannot be the same as the multitude. Rather than worship at the usual shrine, I must climb to the summit to display sincerity and seek the sacred mystery."

sentences.zh: 岳既高峻，人跡罕通。

translations.literal: The peak was lofty and steep; human tracks rarely passed there.
translations.idiomatic: The peak was lofty and steep, and human tracks rarely passed there.

sentences.zh: 武年逾六十，唯將數人攀藤而上，於是稽首祈請。

translations.literal: Wu was over sixty years old; he took only a few men and climbed upward by grasping vines; there he bowed his head and prayed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was over sixty years old. He took only a few men and climbed upward by grasping vines, and there he bowed his head and prayed.

sentences.zh: 晚不得還，即于嶽上藉草而宿。

translations.literal: At evening he could not return and so slept on the peak on piled grass.
translations.idiomatic: At evening he could not return and so slept on the mountain on piled grass.

sentences.zh: 夢一白衣來執武手曰：「快辛苦。」

translations.literal: He dreamed a man in white came, took Wu's hand, and said: "You have toiled greatly."
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed a man in white came, took Wu's hand, and said, "You have toiled greatly."

sentences.zh: 甚相嘉尚。

translations.literal: He showed much admiration for him.
translations.idiomatic: He showed much admiration for him.

sentences.zh: 武遂驚覺，益用祗肅。

translations.literal: Wu awoke with a start and became even more reverent.
translations.idiomatic: Wu awoke with a start and became even more reverent.

sentences.zh: 至旦，雲霧四起，俄而澍雨，遠近沾洽。

translations.literal: At dawn clouds and mist rose on four sides; before long a timely rain fell, soaking the region near and far.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn clouds and mist rose on four sides; before long a timely rain fell, soaking the region near and far.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞之，璽書勞武，賜彩百匹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu heard of it, he sent an imperial letter commending Wu and bestowed a hundred bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu heard of it, he sent an imperial letter commending Wu and bestowed a hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 武性貪吝，其為大司寇也，在庫有萬釘金帶，當時寶之，武因入庫，乃取以歸。

translations.literal: Wu’s nature was greedy and stingy. When he served as Grand Minister of Justice, there was in the storehouse a gold belt with ten thousand studs, which was treasured at the time; when Wu entered the storehouse, he took it and brought it home.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was greedy and miserly by nature. While serving as Grand Minister of Justice, he saw in the storehouse a gold belt with ten thousand studs, prized at the time, and took it home.

sentences.zh: 主得白晉公護，護以武勳重，不彰其過，因而賜之。

translations.literal: The keeper reported this to Hu, Duke of Jin; Hu, because Wu’s merits were weighty, did not expose his fault and consequently bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: The keeper reported it to Yuwen Hu, Duke of Jin. Because Wu’s merits were great, Hu did not expose the offense and instead formally bestowed the belt on him.

sentences.zh: 時論深鄙焉。

translations.literal: Opinion at the time deeply despised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion deeply despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太傅、十五州諸軍事、同州刺史，諡曰桓。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted Grand Mentor, military affairs of fifteen provinces, and Inspector of Tongzhou, and his posthumous name was Huan.
translations.idiomatic: At his death, he was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor, commander of military affairs for fifteen provinces, and Inspector of Tongzhou, with the posthumous name Huan.

sentences.zh: 子震嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhen succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 震字猛略。

translations.literal: Zhen, style name Menglue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, courtesy name Menglue.

sentences.zh: 少驍勇，走及奔馬。

translations.literal: In youth he was fierce and brave and could run as fast as a galloping horse.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was fierce and brave and could run as fast as a galloping horse.

sentences.zh: 周文嘗於渭北校獵，時有兔過周文前，震與諸將競射之，馬倒而墜。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou once held a hunt north of the Wei River; when a rabbit ran before Emperor Wen, Zhen and the other generals competed to shoot it; Zhen's horse fell and he tumbled off.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou once held a hunt north of the Wei River. When a rabbit ran before him, Zhen and the other generals competed to shoot it. Zhen's horse fell and he tumbled off.

sentences.zh: 震足不傾躓，因步走射之，一發中兔。

translations.literal: Zhen's feet did not falter; he walked and shot on foot and with one shot hit the rabbit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's feet did not falter; he walked and shot on foot, and with one shot hit the rabbit.

sentences.zh: 顧馬才起，遂回身騰上。

translations.literal: When he looked back the horse had just risen; he turned and leaped back into the saddle.
translations.idiomatic: When he looked back, the horse had just risen; he turned and leaped back into the saddle.

sentences.zh: 周文喜曰：「非此父不生此子。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said with delight: "Without such a father, such a son would not be born."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said with delight, "Without such a father, such a son would not be born."

sentences.zh: 乃賜震雜彩一百段。

translations.literal: He then bestowed on Zhen a hundred rolls of mixed colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: He then bestowed on Zhen a hundred rolls of mixed colored silk.

sentences.zh: 後封魏昌縣公。

translations.literal: Later he was enfeoffed as Duke of Weichang county.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was enfeoffed as Duke of Weichang.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，拜司右中大夫，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ming reign, he was appointed Director of the Right in the Ministry of Works, with the additional titles Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Ming reign, he was appointed Director of the Right in the Ministry of Works, with the additional titles Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 武成初，進爵廣平郡公，除華州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wucheng reign, his rank was advanced to Duke of Guangping commandery and he was appointed Regional Inspector of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wucheng reign, his rank was advanced to Duke of Guangping and he was appointed Regional Inspector of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 震雖出自膏腴，少習武藝，然頗有政術。

translations.literal: Although Zhen came from a wealthy family and had learned military arts from youth, he nevertheless possessed considerable skill in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Although Zhen came from a wealthy family and had learned military arts from youth, he nevertheless possessed considerable skill in governance.

sentences.zh: 天和六年，拜柱國。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe, he was appointed pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhe, he was appointed Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 建德初，襲爵鄭國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande, he inherited the title Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jiande, he inherited the title Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 從平鄴，賜妾二人、女樂一部，拜大宗伯。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Ye, he was granted two concubines and a company of female musicians and was appointed Grand Director of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Ye, he was granted two concubines and a company of female musicians and was appointed Grand Director of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 震父嘗為此職，時論榮之。

translations.literal: Zhen's father had once held this office; at the time opinion counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's father had once held this office; at the time opinion counted it an honor.

sentences.zh: 宣政中，出為原州總管。

translations.literal: During the Xuanzheng period, he went out as Grand Governor of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuanzheng period, he went out as Grand Governor of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，薨於家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang in Sui, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang in Sui, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 震弟惎，大象末，為益州刺史，與王謙據蜀起兵，被誅。

translations.literal: Zhen's younger brother Ji, at the end of the Daxiang reign, was Regional Inspector of Yizhou; he joined Wang Qian in raising troops and holding Shu, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's younger brother Ji, at the end of the Daxiang reign, was Regional Inspector of Yizhou. He joined Wang Qian in raising troops and holding Shu, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 若干惠，字惠保，代武川人也。

translations.literal: Ruo Ganhui, style name Huibao, was a man of Wuchuan in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Ruo Ganhui, courtesy name Huibao, was a native of Wuchuan in Dai.

sentences.zh: 其先與魏俱起，以國為姓。

translations.literal: His ancestors had risen together with Wei and took the state name as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had risen together with Wei and took the state name as their surname.

sentences.zh: 父樹利周，從魏廣陽王深征葛榮，戰沒，贈冀州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Shulizhou followed Prince Shen of Guangyang of Wei in campaigning against Ge Rong, died in battle, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Regional Inspector of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shulizhou followed Prince Shen of Guangyang of Wei in campaigning against Ge Rong, died in battle, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Regional Inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 惠以別將從賀拔嶽，以功封北平縣男。

translations.literal: Hui as separate commander followed Heba Yue and by merit was enfeoffed as Baron of Beiping county.
translations.idiomatic: Hui served as a separate commander under Heba Yue and by merit was enfeoffed as Baron of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 及岳為侯莫陳悅所害，惠與寇洛、趙貴等同謀翊戴周文。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, Hui together with Kou Luo, Zhao Gui, and others jointly plotted to support and install Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, Hui together with Kou Luo, Zhao Gui, and others jointly plotted to support and install Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 仍從平悅，拜直閣將軍。

translations.literal: He still followed in pacifying Yue and was appointed General of the Direct Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He still followed in pacifying Yue and was appointed General of the Direct Gate.

sentences.zh: 從禽竇泰，復弘農，破沙苑，惠每先登陷陣。

translations.literal: He followed in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and breaking Shaya; in each case Hui was first to ascend and break through the enemy lines.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and breaking Shaya; in each case Hui was first to ascend and break through the enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 加侍中、開府儀同三司、封長樂郡公。

translations.literal: He was given the additional titles Palace Attendant, Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, and Duke of Changle commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional titles Palace Attendant, Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, and Duke of Changle.

sentences.zh: 大統四年，從魏文帝東巡洛陽，與齊神武戰於河橋，力戰破之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong, he followed Emperor Wen of Wei on the eastern tour to Luoyang and fought Qi Shenwu at Heqiao, fighting fiercely and defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Datong, he followed Emperor Wen of Wei on the eastern tour to Luoyang and fought Gao Huan at Heqiao, fighting fiercely and defeating him.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷領軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was transferred to Commander of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, he was transferred to Commander of the Army.

sentences.zh: 及高仲密舉北豫州來附，周文迎之。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi raised Beiyu province and came over, Emperor Wen of Zhou went to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi raised Beiyu province and defected, Emperor Wen of Zhou went to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 軍至洛陽，齊神武屯於芒山。

translations.literal: When the army reached Luoyang, Qi Shenwu encamped at Mangshan.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Luoyang, Gao Huan encamped at Mangshan.

sentences.zh: 惠為右軍，與中軍大破之。

translations.literal: Hui commanded the right wing and together with the center army thoroughly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Hui commanded the right wing and together with the center army thoroughly defeated them.

sentences.zh: 齊神武兵乃萃左軍，軍將趙貴等戰不利。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu's troops then massed against the left wing; the generals Zhao Gui and others fought without success.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan's troops then massed against the left wing; the generals Zhao Gui and others fought without success.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，齊神武進兵攻惠，惠擊之，皆披靡。

translations.literal: Just then dusk fell; Qi Shenwu advanced troops to attack Hui; Hui struck them and all were routed.
translations.idiomatic: As dusk fell, Gao Huan advanced to attack Hui. Hui struck back and routed them all.

sentences.zh: 至夜中，神武騎復來追惠。

translations.literal: By midnight Shenwu's cavalry again came in pursuit of Hui.
translations.idiomatic: By midnight Gao Huan's cavalry came in pursuit of Hui again.

sentences.zh: 惠徐下馬，顧命廚人營食。

translations.literal: Hui slowly dismounted and ordered the cook to prepare food.
translations.idiomatic: Hui slowly dismounted and ordered the cook to prepare a meal.

sentences.zh: 食訖，謂左右曰：「長安死，此中死，異乎？」

translations.literal: When the meal was finished, he said to those beside him: "To die in Chang'an or to die here—what difference is there?"
translations.idiomatic: When the meal was finished, he said to those beside him, "To die in Chang'an or to die here—what difference is there?"

sentences.zh: 乃建旗鳴角，收軍而還。

translations.literal: He then raised banners and sounded horns, recalled the army, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised banners and sounded horns, recalled the army, and returned.

sentences.zh: 神武追騎憚惠，疑有伏兵，不敢逼。

translations.literal: Shenwu's pursuing cavalry feared Hui, suspected an ambush, and did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan's pursuing cavalry feared Hui, suspected an ambush, and did not dare press close.

sentences.zh: 至弘農，見周文，陳賊形勢，恨其垂成之功，虧於一簣，噓唏不自勝。

translations.literal: When he reached Hongnong and saw Emperor Wen of Zhou, he reported the enemy situation, regretting that his nearly completed achievement had failed for want of one basketful of earth, and sighed uncontrollably.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Hongnong and saw Emperor Wen of Zhou, he reported the enemy situation, grieving that victory had slipped away at the last moment, and sighed uncontrollably.

sentences.zh: 周文壯之，遷司空。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen admired him and transferred him to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen admired him and appointed him Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 惠性剛質，有勇力，容貌魁岸。

translations.literal: Hui's nature was firm and straightforward; he had courage and strength, and his appearance was imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was firm and straightforward by nature, possessed courage and strength, and had an imposing appearance.

sentences.zh: 善於撫禦，將士莫不懷恩。

translations.literal: He was skilled at comforting and controlling troops; officers and soldiers all cherished his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at winning over and commanding his troops; officers and soldiers alike cherished his kindness.

sentences.zh: 及侯景內附，朝議欲收輯河南，令惠以本官鎮魯陽。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing came over to the interior, court deliberation wished to gather and secure Henan and ordered Hui with his existing office to garrison Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing defected to the Zhou, the court resolved to secure Henan and ordered Hui, retaining his existing office, to garrison Luyang.

sentences.zh: 遇病，薨於軍。

translations.literal: He fell ill and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 惠于諸將年最少。

translations.literal: Among the generals, Hui was the youngest.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was the youngest of the generals.

sentences.zh: 早喪父，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: He lost his father early and was known for serving his mother with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father early and became known for filial service to his mother.

sentences.zh: 周文嘗造射堂新成，與諸將宴射。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou once built a shooting hall, and when it was newly completed, he feasted and practiced archery with the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou once had an archery hall built, and when it was newly finished, he feasted and shot there with the generals.

sentences.zh: 惠竊歎曰：「親老矣，何時辦此！」

translations.literal: Hui privately sighed and said, “My parent is old. When will I ever manage to provide this!”
translations.idiomatic: Hui privately sighed, “My mother is old. When will I ever be able to provide this!”

sentences.zh: 周文聞之，即日徙堂于惠宅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou heard of this, he moved the hall to Hui’s residence that very day.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou heard this, he had the hall moved to Hui’s residence that same day.

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem shown to him.

sentences.zh: 及薨，為流涕久之。

translations.literal: When Hui died, Emperor Wen shed tears for him for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui died, Emperor Wen wept for him for a long time.

sentences.zh: 惠喪至，又臨撫焉。

translations.literal: When Hui’s funeral bier arrived, he again visited and consoled it.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui’s coffin arrived, he again came in person to mourn and comfort the family.

sentences.zh: 加贈秦州刺史，諡曰武烈。

translations.literal: He was additionally posthumously granted Inspector of Qinzhou, and his posthumous name was Wulie.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was additionally honored as Inspector of Qinzhou, with the posthumous name Wulie.

sentences.zh: 子鳳嗣。

translations.literal: His son Feng succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feng inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 鳳字達摩，有識度。

translations.literal: Feng, style name Damo, had discernment and breadth of view.
translations.idiomatic: Feng, courtesy name Damo, was a man of discernment and breadth of view.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵長樂郡公，尚周文女。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's title Duke of Changle commandery and married a daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's title Duke of Changle and married a daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 位開府儀同三司、大馭中大夫。

translations.literal: His posts were Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and Director in the Ministry of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and Director in the Ministry of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 後錄惠佐命功，封鳳徐國公，拜柱國。

translations.literal: Later, recording Hui's merit in assisting the founding, Feng was enfeoffed as Duke of Xu and appointed pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in recognition of Hui's merit in assisting the founding, Feng was enfeoffed as Duke of Xu and appointed Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 怡峰，字景阜，遼西人也。

translations.literal: Yi Feng, style name Jingfu, was a man of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Feng, courtesy name Jingfu, was a native of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 本姓默台，因避難改焉。

translations.literal: His original surname was Motai; because of taking refuge from troubles he changed it.
translations.idiomatic: His original surname was Motai; he changed it when he took refuge from turmoil.

sentences.zh: 高祖寬，燕遼西郡守，魏道武時歸朝，拜羽真，賜爵長蛇公。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Kuan was Administrator of Liaoxi commandery in Yan; at the time of Emperor Daowu of Wei he submitted to the court, was appointed yuzhen, and was granted the title Duke of Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Kuan was Administrator of Liaoxi in Yan. At the time of Emperor Daowu of Wei he submitted to the court, was appointed yuzhen, and was granted the title Duke of Changshe.

sentences.zh: 曾祖文，冀州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Wen was Regional Inspector of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Wen served as Regional Inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 峰少以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: Feng in youth was known for fierce bravery.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Feng was known for fierce bravery.

sentences.zh: 從賀拔岳討万俟醜奴，賜爵蒲陰縣男。

translations.literal: He followed Heba Yue in campaigning against Moqi Chounu and was granted the title Baron of Puyin county.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Heba Yue in campaigning against Moqi Chounu and was granted the title Baron of Puyin.

sentences.zh: 岳被害，峰與趙貴等同謀翊戴周文，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed, Feng together with Zhao Gui and others jointly plotted to support and install Emperor Wen of Zhou, and his rank was advanced to count.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was killed, Feng together with Zhao Gui and others jointly plotted to support and install Emperor Wen of Zhou, and his rank was advanced to count.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武與孝武帝構隙，文帝令峰與都督趙貴赴洛陽。

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu and Emperor Xiaowu of Wei fell into discord, Emperor Wen ordered Feng together with Commander-in-chief Zhao Gui to go to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan and Emperor Xiaowu of Wei fell into discord, Emperor Wen ordered Feng and Commander-in-chief Zhao Gui to go to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 至潼關，孝武西遷，峰即從周文帝拔回洛，復潼關。

translations.literal: When they reached Tong Pass, Emperor Xiaowu moved west; Feng then followed Emperor Wen of Zhou in retaking Luoyang and recovering Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Tong Pass, Emperor Xiaowu moved west. Feng then followed Emperor Wen of Zhou in retaking Luoyang and recovering Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 後以討曹泥功，進爵華陽縣公。

translations.literal: Later, for merit in campaigning against Cao Ni, his rank was advanced to Duke of Huayang county.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for merit in campaigning against Cao Ni, his rank was advanced to Duke of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 又從破竇泰于小關。

translations.literal: Again he followed in defeating Dou Tai at Xiaoguan.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed in defeating Dou Tai at Xiaoguan.

sentences.zh: 復弘農，破沙苑，進爵樂陵郡公。

translations.literal: He recovered Hongnong and broke Shaya; his rank was advanced to Duke of Leling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Hongnong and broke Shaya, and his rank was advanced to Duke of Leling.

sentences.zh: 仍與元季海、獨孤信復洛陽。

translations.literal: He still together with Yuan Jihai and Dugu Xin recovered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Yuan Jihai and Dugu Xin in recovering Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 東魏行台任祥率步騎萬餘攻潁川，峰復以輕騎五百邀擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Ren Xiang, Eastern Wei mobile headquarters commander, led more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Yingchuan; Feng again with five hundred light cavalry intercepted and struck them and thoroughly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Xiang, Eastern Wei mobile headquarters commander, led more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Yingchuan. Feng again intercepted them with five hundred light cavalry and routed them.

sentences.zh: 自是威名轉盛。

translations.literal: From this his martial renown grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: From this his martial renown grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 加授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was additionally granted Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally granted the title Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 及周文與東魏戰河橋，時峰為左軍，不利，與李遠先還，周文遂班師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou fought Eastern Wei at Heqiao, at the time Feng commanded the left wing; it went badly; he together with Li Yuan returned first, and Emperor Wen thereupon withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou fought Eastern Wei at Heqiao, Feng commanded the left wing. The battle went badly, and he returned ahead with Li Yuan, whereupon Emperor Wen withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 詔原其罪。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned his offense.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned his offense.

sentences.zh: 拜夏州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regional Inspector of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Regional Inspector of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 大統十五年，東魏圍潁川，峰與趙貴赴援。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Datong, Eastern Wei besieged Yingchuan; Feng together with Zhao Gui went to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Datong, Eastern Wei besieged Yingchuan. Feng and Zhao Gui went to the relief.

sentences.zh: 至南陽，病卒。

translations.literal: When he reached Nanyang, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Nanyang, he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 峰沈毅有膽略，得士卒心，當時號驍將。

translations.literal: Feng was steady and resolute and had courage and strategy; he won the hearts of officers and soldiers, and at the time was called a fierce general.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was steady and resolute, possessed courage and strategy, and won the hearts of officers and soldiers. At the time he was known as a fierce general.

sentences.zh: 周文嗟悼者久之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou mourned and lamented for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou mourned him for a long time.

sentences.zh: 贈華州刺史，諡曰襄威。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Regional Inspector of Huazhou, with posthumous title Xiangwei.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Regional Inspector of Huazhou, with the posthumous title Xiangwei.

sentences.zh: 子昂嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 位開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His post was Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 朝廷追錄峰功，封昂郡公。

translations.literal: The court posthumously recorded Feng's merit and enfeoffed Ang as Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously recorded Feng's merit and enfeoffed Ang as a commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 昂弟光，少以峰勳，賜爵安平縣侯，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Ang's younger brother Guang, in youth because of Feng's merit, was granted the title Marquis of Anping county and given the additional title Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's younger brother Guang, by virtue of Feng's merit from youth, was granted the title Marquis of Anping and given the additional title Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 光弟春，少知名，位吏部下大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Guang's younger brother Chun was known from youth; his posts were Director in the Ministry of Personnel and ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's younger brother Chun was known from youth. He held the posts of Director in the Ministry of Personnel and ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 劉亮，中山人也，本名道德。

translations.literal: Liu Liang was a man of Zhongshan; his original name was Daode.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang was a native of Zhongshan; his original name was Daode.

sentences.zh: 父特真，位領人酋長。

translations.literal: His father Tezhen held the post of tribal chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tezhen held the post of tribal chieftain.

sentences.zh: 魏大統中，以亮著勳，追贈恆州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Datong era of Wei, because of Liang's outstanding merit, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Regional Inspector of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Datong era of Wei, because of Liang's outstanding merit, his father was posthumously enfeoffed as Regional Inspector of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 亮少倜儻，有從橫計略，姿貌魁傑，見者憚之。

translations.literal: Liang in youth was bold and free-spirited and had stratagems of alliance and opposition; his appearance was towering and outstanding, and those who saw him feared him.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Liang was bold and free-spirited and possessed stratagems of alliance and opposition. His appearance was towering and outstanding, and those who saw him feared him.

sentences.zh: 以都督從賀拔嶽西征，以功封廣興縣子。

translations.literal: As commander he followed Heba Yue on the western campaign and by merit was enfeoffed as Viscount of Guangxing county.
translations.idiomatic: As commander he followed Heba Yue on the western campaign and by merit was enfeoffed as Viscount of Guangxing.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳悅害嶽，亮與諸將謀迎周文。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue killed Yue; Liang together with the generals plotted to welcome Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Houmochen Yue killed Yue, Liang and the other generals plotted to welcome Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 及平悅後，悅党豳州刺史孫定兒仍據州不下，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: After pacifying Yue, Yue's partisan Sun Ding'er, Regional Inspector of Binzhou, still held the province and would not submit; his followers reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue was pacified, Yue's partisan Sun Ding'er, Regional Inspector of Binzhou, still held the province and would not submit. His followers numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 周文令亮襲之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou ordered Liang to raid him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou ordered Liang to raid him.

sentences.zh: 定兒以義兵猶遠，未為之備。

translations.literal: Ding'er because the relief army was still far away did not prepare against it.
translations.idiomatic: Ding'er, thinking the relief army was still far away, made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 亮乃輕將二十騎，先豎一纛于近城高嶺，即馳入城中。

translations.literal: Liang then lightly took twenty horsemen, first erected a banner on a high ridge near the city, and immediately galloped into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liang then took only twenty horsemen, first erected a banner on a high ridge near the city, and immediately galloped into the city.

sentences.zh: 定兒方置酒高會，卒見亮至，眾皆駭愕。

translations.literal: Ding'er was just holding a grand banquet with wine when suddenly he saw Liang arrive; the crowd all were struck with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Ding'er was just holding a grand banquet when suddenly he saw Liang arrive. The crowd was struck with alarm.

sentences.zh: 亮乃麾兵斬定兒，懸首州門，號令賊黨。

translations.literal: Liang then commanded troops to behead Ding'er, hung the head at the provincial gate, and issued orders to the rebel band.
translations.idiomatic: Liang then commanded his troops to behead Ding'er, hung the head at the provincial gate, and issued orders to the rebel band.

sentences.zh: 仍遙指城外纛，命二騎曰：「出追大軍。」

translations.literal: He then pointed from afar to the banner outside the city and ordered two horsemen: "Go out and pursue the great army."
translations.idiomatic: He then pointed from afar to the banner outside the city and ordered two horsemen, "Go out and pursue the main army."

sentences.zh: 賊党兇懼，一時降服。

translations.literal: The rebel band, fierce and fearful, all at once submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel band, fierce and fearful, submitted all at once.

sentences.zh: 及周文置十二軍，簡諸將領之，亮領一軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou established the twelve armies and selected generals to command them, Liang commanded one army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou established the twelve armies and selected generals to command them, Liang commanded one army.

sentences.zh: 每征討，常與怡峰俱為騎將。

translations.literal: On every campaign he was regularly together with Yi Feng as cavalry generals.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign he regularly served as cavalry general together with Yi Feng.

sentences.zh: 以復潼關功，封饒陽縣伯。

translations.literal: For merit in recovering Tong Pass, he was enfeoffed as Count of Raoyang county.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in recovering Tong Pass, he was enfeoffed as Count of Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 尋加侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional title Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the additional title Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 從禽竇泰，復弘農，虞沙苑，並力戰有功。

translations.literal: He followed in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and at Shaya; in each he fought fiercely with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and fighting at Shaya; in each case he fought fiercely with distinction.

sentences.zh: 遷開府儀同三司、大都督，進爵長廣公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and Grand Commander, and his rank was advanced to Duke of Changguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and Grand Commander, and his rank was advanced to Duke of Changguang.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職，居喪毀瘠。

translations.literal: Because of mourning for his mother he left office; in observing mourning he wasted away.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother and wasted away in grief.

sentences.zh: 周文嗟其至性，每憂惜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou sighed at his utmost filial nature and always worried and cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou sighed at his utmost filial devotion and always worried over him.

sentences.zh: 起復本官。

translations.literal: He was recalled to his original office before mourning ended.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to his original office before mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 亮以勇敢見知，為當時名將，兼屢陳謀策，多合機宜。

translations.literal: Liang was recognized for courage and was a famous general of the time; moreover he repeatedly offered stratagems, most of which accorded with the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was recognized for courage and was a famous general of the time. He also repeatedly offered stratagems, most of which accorded with the opportune moment.

sentences.zh: 周文謂曰：「卿文武兼資，即孤之孔明也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou said to him: "You possess both civil and military gifts—you are my Kongming."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou said to him, "You possess both civil and military gifts—you are my Kongming."

sentences.zh: 乃賜名亮，並賜姓侯莫陳氏。

translations.literal: He then granted him the name Liang and also granted him the surname Houmochen.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted him the name Liang and also granted him the surname Houmochen.

sentences.zh: 出為東雍州刺史，為政清靜，百姓安之。

translations.literal: He went out as Regional Inspector of Dongyong and governed with quiet integrity; the common people were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Regional Inspector of Dongyong and governed with quiet integrity; the common people lived in peace under him.

sentences.zh: 卒於州。

translations.literal: He died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 喪還京，周文親臨之，泣而謂人曰：「股肱喪矣，腹心何寄！」

translations.literal: When the coffin returned to the capital, Emperor Wen of Zhou came in person; weeping he said to others: "My arms and legs are lost—where shall I place my heart!"
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin returned to the capital, Emperor Wen of Zhou came in person. Weeping, he said to others, "My arms and legs are lost—where shall I place my heart!"

sentences.zh: 令鴻臚卿臨護喪事，追贈太尉，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: He ordered the Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments to oversee the funeral; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Commandant with posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments to oversee the funeral. Liang was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Commandant, with the posthumous title Xiang.

sentences.zh: 後配餉周文廟廷。

translations.literal: Later he was paired for offerings in the temple hall of Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was paired for offerings in the temple hall of Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 子昶嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 昶尚周文女西河長公主，大象中，位柱國、秦靈二州總管，以亮功封彭國公。

translations.literal: Chang married the Princess Chang of Xihe, daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou; in the Daxiang era his posts were pillar of state and Grand Governor of Qin and Ling provinces; because of Liang's merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Peng.
translations.idiomatic: Chang married the Princess Chang of Xihe, daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou. In the Daxiang era he held the posts of Pillar of State and Grand Governor of Qin and Ling provinces, and because of Liang's merit was enfeoffed as Duke of Peng.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，坐事死。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui, he was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui, he was executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 昶弟靜，天水郡守。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Jing was Administrator of Tianshui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's younger brother Jing was Administrator of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 靜弟恭，開府儀同三司、饒陽縣伯。

translations.literal: Jing's younger brother Gong held Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and was Count of Raoyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's younger brother Gong held the title Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and was Count of Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 恭弟幹，上儀同三司、褒中侯。

translations.literal: Gong's younger brother Gan held ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and was Marquis of Baozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's younger brother Gan held ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and was Marquis of Baozhong.

sentences.zh: 王德，字天恩，代武川人也。

translations.literal: Wang De, courtesy name Tian’en, was a man of Wuchuan in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De, styled Tian’en, was from Wuchuan in Dai.

sentences.zh: 少善騎射，雖不經師訓，以孝悌稱。

translations.literal: From youth he was skilled in riding and archery; although he had not passed through a teacher’s instruction, he was praised for filial piety and fraternal respect.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was skilled at riding and archery. Though he had no formal education, he was praised for filial and fraternal conduct.

sentences.zh: 初從爾硃榮討元顥，賜爵同官縣子。

translations.literal: At first he followed Erzhu Rong in attacking Yuan Hao and was granted the title Viscount of Tongguan County.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed Erzhu Rong against Yuan Hao and was granted the title Viscount of Tongguan County.

sentences.zh: 又從賀拔岳討平万俟醜奴，別封深澤縣男。

translations.literal: He also followed Heba Yue in attacking and pacifying Moqi Chounu, and was separately enfeoffed as Baron of Shenze County.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Heba Yue in defeating Moqi Chounu and was separately enfeoffed Baron of Shenze County.

sentences.zh: 及侯莫陳悅害嶽，德與寇洛等議，翊戴周文，於是除平涼郡守。

translations.literal: When Houmochen Yue killed Yue, De discussed matters with Kou Luo and others, supported and enthroned Emperor Wen of Zhou, and was then appointed Governor of Pingliang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Houmochen Yue killed Heba Yue, De consulted with Kou Luo and others and supported Emperor Wen of Zhou, after which he was appointed Governor of Pingliang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 德雖不知書，至於斷決處分，良吏無以過。

translations.literal: Although De did not know books, when it came to judgments and decisions, good officials could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Although De was not learned, in deciding cases and handling affairs even able officials could not surpass him.

sentences.zh: 涇州所部五郡，德常為最。

translations.literal: Among the five commanderies under Jingzhou, De was always ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Among the five commanderies under Jingzhou, De was always rated the best.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，進封下博縣伯，行東雍州事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, De was advanced in fief to Earl of Xiabo County and acted in charge of East Yongzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, De was promoted to Earl of Xiabo County and made acting head of East Yongzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 在州未幾，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: He had not been in the province long before the people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He had been in the province only a short time before the people grew attached to him.

sentences.zh: 賜姓烏丸氏。

translations.literal: He was granted the surname Wuwan.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the surname Wuwan.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，進爵為公，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司、北雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong, his title was advanced to duke, and he was additionally made General-in-Chief of Chariots and Cavalry, granted Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies, and appointed Inspector of North Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong, he was advanced to duke and additionally appointed General-in-Chief of Chariots and Cavalry, granted Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies, and made Inspector of North Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 後常從周文征伐，累有戰功，加開府、侍中，進爵河間郡公。

translations.literal: Later he regularly followed Emperor Wen of Zhou on campaigns, repeatedly had battle merit, was additionally granted Opening Office and Palace Attendant, and his title was advanced to Duke of Hejian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he regularly accompanied Emperor Wen of Zhou on campaign, repeatedly winning battle honors. He was additionally granted Opening Office and Palace Attendant, and advanced to Duke of Hejian Commandery.

sentences.zh: 先是河、渭間種羌屢叛，以德有威名，拜河州刺史。

translations.literal: Previously the various Qiang between the Yellow River and Wei River had repeatedly rebelled; because De had a reputation for authority, he was appointed Inspector of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang groups between the Yellow River and the Wei had repeatedly rebelled, so because De had a reputation for authority, he was appointed Inspector of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 群羌率服。

translations.literal: The Qiang groups all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang groups all submitted.

sentences.zh: 後卒于涇州刺史，諡曰獻。

translations.literal: Later he died as Inspector of Jingzhou, and his posthumous name was Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died while serving as Inspector of Jingzhou, with the posthumous name Xian.

sentences.zh: 德性厚重廉慎，言行無擇。

translations.literal: De’s nature was generous, grave, honest, and cautious, and there was nothing to criticize in his words and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: De was generous, grave, honest, and cautious by nature; nothing in his words or actions invited criticism.

sentences.zh: 母幾年百歲，後德終。

translations.literal: His mother was nearly one hundred sui old and died after De.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was nearly one hundred and died after De.

sentences.zh: 子慶嗣，小名公奴。

translations.literal: His son Qing succeeded; his childhood name was Gongnu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qing succeeded him; his childhood name was Gongnu.

sentences.zh: 性謹厚，位開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His nature was careful and honest; his post was Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was careful and honest by nature and held the post of Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 初德喪父，貧無以葬，乃賣公奴並一女以營葬事。

translations.literal: When De first lost his father, he was too poor to bury him and so sold Gongnu together with one daughter to arrange the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When De first lost his father, he was too poor to bury him and so sold Gongnu together with one daughter to arrange the funeral.

sentences.zh: 因遭兵亂，不復相知。

translations.literal: Because of encountering military turmoil, they no longer knew one another.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the military turmoil, they lost contact with one another.

sentences.zh: 及德在平涼，始得之，遂名曰慶。

translations.literal: When De was at Pingliang, he finally found him and so named him Qing.
translations.idiomatic: When De was at Pingliang, he finally found him and named him Qing.

sentences.zh: 赫連達，字朔周，盛樂人，勃勃之後也。

translations.literal: He Lianda, style name Shuozhou, was a man of Shengle and a descendant of Bobo.
translations.idiomatic: He Lianda, courtesy name Shuozhou, was a native of Shengle and a descendant of Bobo.

sentences.zh: 曾祖庫多汗，因避難改姓杜氏。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Kuduo Han, because of taking refuge from troubles, changed his surname to Du.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Kuduo Han changed his surname to Du when he took refuge from turmoil.

sentences.zh: 達性剛鯁有膽力。

translations.literal: Da's nature was firm and upright and he had courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Da was firm and upright by nature and possessed courage and strength.

sentences.zh: 少從賀拔岳征討有功，賜爵長廣鄉男。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Heba Yue on campaigns with merit and was granted the title Baron of Changguang township.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he followed Heba Yue on campaigns with distinction and was granted the title Baron of Changguang township.

sentences.zh: 及岳為侯莫陳悅所害，趙貴建議迎周文，達贊成其議，請輕騎告周文，仍迎之。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, Zhao Gui proposed welcoming Emperor Wen of Zhou; Da approved the plan, requested light cavalry to inform Emperor Wen, and still went to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, Zhao Gui proposed welcoming Emperor Wen of Zhou. Da approved the plan, asked to ride ahead with light cavalry to inform Emperor Wen, and then went to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 諸將或欲南追賀拔勝，或云東告朝廷。

translations.literal: Some of the generals wished to pursue Heba Sheng to the south, or said they should report east to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Some of the generals wished to pursue Heba Sheng to the south, while others said they should report east to the court.

sentences.zh: 達又曰：「此皆遠水不救近火，何足道哉！」

translations.literal: Da again said: "These are all distant water that cannot save a nearby fire—what is there to say of them!"
translations.idiomatic: Da again said, "These are all distant water that cannot save a nearby fire—what is there to say of them!"

sentences.zh: 謀遂定，令達馳往。

translations.literal: The plan was then settled and Da was ordered to gallop there.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was then settled, and Da was ordered to gallop ahead.

sentences.zh: 周文見達慟哭，遂以數百騎南赴平涼，令達率騎據彈箏峽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou saw Da he wept bitterly; he then with several hundred horsemen hurried south to Pingliang and ordered Da to lead cavalry to hold Tanzheng Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou saw Da he wept bitterly. He then hurried south to Pingliang with several hundred horsemen and ordered Da to lead cavalry to hold Tanzheng Pass.

sentences.zh: 時百姓惶懼奔散者，軍爭欲掠之。

translations.literal: At the time the common people, fearful and fleeing in dispersion, were what the army all wished to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the common people were fleeing in fear and dispersion, and the army all wished to plunder them.

sentences.zh: 達止之，乃撫以恩信，人皆悅附。

translations.literal: Da stopped them and then comforted the people with kindness and trust; all gladly attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Da stopped them and comforted the people with kindness and trust; all gladly attached themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 周文聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou heard of it he commended him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou heard of it he commended him.

sentences.zh: 加平東將軍。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 周文謂諸將曰：「當清水公遇禍之日，君等性命懸於賊手。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou said to the generals: "On the day when Duke of Qingshui met disaster, your lives hung in the hands of the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou said to the generals, "On the day when Duke of Qingshui met disaster, your lives hung in the hands of the bandits.

sentences.zh: 杜朔周冒萬死之難，遠來見及，遂得同雪讎恥。

translations.literal: Du Shuozhou braved the peril of ten thousand deaths, came from afar to reach us, and thus we were able together to wipe away the shame of vengeance.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shuozhou braved mortal peril, came from afar to reach us, and thus together we were able to avenge our shame.

sentences.zh: 勞而不酬，何以勸善？」

translations.literal: To labor without reward—how can one encourage good?"
translations.idiomatic: To labor without reward—how can one encourage good deeds?"

sentences.zh: 乃賜馬二百疋。

translations.literal: He then bestowed two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: He then bestowed two hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 孝武入關，褒敘勳義，以達首迎元帥，匡復秦、隴，進爵魏昌縣伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered the Pass, merit and righteousness were commended; because Da was first to welcome the commander-in-chief and restored Qin and Long, his rank was advanced to Count of Weichang county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu entered the Pass, merit and righteousness were commended. Because Da was first to welcome the commander-in-chief and restored Qin and Long, his rank was advanced to Count of Weichang.

sentences.zh: 從儀同李虎破曹泥。

translations.literal: He followed Opening-general Li Hu in defeating Cao Ni.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Opening-general Li Hu in defeating Cao Ni.

sentences.zh: 後復弘農，戰沙苑，皆有功。

translations.literal: Later he recovered Hongnong and fought at Shaya; in each he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later he recovered Hongnong and fought at Shaya; in each case he distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 詔復姓赫連。

translations.literal: An edict restored his surname to Helian.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored his surname to Helian.

sentences.zh: 以達勳望兼隆，乃除雲州刺史，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Because Da's merit and renown were both lofty, he was appointed Regional Inspector of Yunzhou and his rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Because Da's merit and renown were both lofty, he was appointed Regional Inspector of Yunzhou and his rank was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍達奚武攻漢中。

translations.literal: He followed Grand General Da Xiwu in attacking Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Grand General Da Xiwu in the attack on Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 梁宜豐侯蕭修拒守積時，後乃送款。

translations.literal: Xiao Xiu, Marquis of Yifeng of Liang, resisted and held firm for a long time; afterward he sent over his submission.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xiu, Marquis of Yifeng of Liang, resisted and held firm for a long time before finally submitting.

sentences.zh: 開府賀蘭願德等以其食盡，欲急攻取之。

translations.literal: Opening-general Helan Yuande and others, because their provisions were exhausted, wished to attack quickly and take them.
translations.idiomatic: Opening-general Helan Yuande and others, seeing that their provisions were exhausted, wished to attack quickly and take the city.

sentences.zh: 達曰：「不戰而獲城，策之上也。

translations.literal: Da said: "To take a city without fighting is the highest stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Da said, "To take a city without fighting is the highest stratagem.

sentences.zh: 無容利其子女，貪其財帛，仁者不為。

translations.literal: One must not profit from their sons and daughters or covet their wealth and silk— a benevolent man does not do this.
translations.idiomatic: One must not profit from their sons and daughters or covet their wealth and silk—a benevolent man does not do this.

sentences.zh: 如其困獸猶鬥，則成敗未可知。」

translations.literal: If they fight like cornered beasts, then victory or defeat cannot be known."
translations.idiomatic: If they fight like cornered beasts, the outcome cannot be known."

sentences.zh: 武遂受修降。

translations.literal: Wu then accepted Xiu's surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wu then accepted Xiu's surrender.

sentences.zh: 師還，遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中，進爵藍田縣公。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was transferred to Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, given the additional title Palace Attendant, and advanced to Duke of Lantian county.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was transferred to Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, given the additional title Palace Attendant, and advanced to Duke of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 保定初，為大將軍、夏州總管。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he was Grand General and Grand Governor of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoding, he was Grand General and Grand Governor of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 達雖非文吏，然性質直，遵奉法度，輕於鞭撻，而重慎死罪。

translations.literal: Although Da was not a civil official, his nature was straightforward; he observed the law, was lenient with flogging, yet was cautious with capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Although Da was not a civil official, he was straightforward by nature, observed the law, was lenient with flogging, yet was cautious with capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 性又廉儉。

translations.literal: His nature was also frugal and modest.
translations.idiomatic: He was also frugal and modest by nature.

sentences.zh: 邊境胡人或饋達羊，達欲招異類，報以繒帛。

translations.literal: Barbarians on the border sometimes presented sheep to Da; Da wished to win over foreign peoples and repaid them with silk.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians on the border sometimes presented sheep to Da. Wishing to win over foreign peoples, he repaid them with silk.

sentences.zh: 主司請用官物。

translations.literal: The responsible official requested to use government goods.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible official requested to use government goods.

sentences.zh: 達曰：「羊入我廚，物出官庫，是欺上也。」

translations.literal: Da said: "Sheep enter my kitchen but goods come from the official storehouse—this is deceiving one's superiors."
translations.idiomatic: Da said, "Sheep enter my kitchen but goods come from the official storehouse—this is deceiving one's superiors."

sentences.zh: 命取私帛與之。

translations.literal: He ordered his private silk taken and given to them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his private silk taken and given to them.

sentences.zh: 識者嘉其仁恕。

translations.literal: Those of discernment praised his benevolence and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Those of discernment praised his benevolence and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 尋進爵樂川郡公，位柱國。

translations.literal: Soon his rank was advanced to Duke of Yuechuan commandery and his post was pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his rank was advanced to Duke of Yuechuan and he was appointed Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子遷嗣。

translations.literal: His son Qian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 位大將軍、蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: His posts were Grand General and Regional Inspector of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of Grand General and Regional Inspector of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 韓果，字阿六拔，代武川人也。

translations.literal: Han Guo, style name Aluoba, was a man of Wuchuan in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Han Guo, courtesy name Aluoba, was a native of Wuchuan in Dai.

sentences.zh: 少驍雄，善騎射。

translations.literal: In youth he was fierce and heroic and skilled at riding and shooting.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was fierce and heroic and skilled at riding and shooting.

sentences.zh: 賀拔嶽西征，引為帳內，擊万俟醜奴。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue campaigned west, he was brought into the tent guard and struck Moqi Chounu.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue campaigned west, he was brought into the tent guard and fought Moqi Chounu.

sentences.zh: 後從周文討平侯莫陳悅。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Wen of Zhou in campaigning to pacify Houmochen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Emperor Wen of Zhou in campaigning to pacify Houmochen Yue.

sentences.zh: 大統初，累進爵為石城公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, by repeated advancement his rank became Duke of Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Datong, by repeated advancement his rank became Duke of Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 果性強記，兼有權略，善伺敵虛實，揣知情狀。

translations.literal: Guo's nature was strongly retentive of memory; he also had stratagem and scheme, was skilled at observing the enemy's strengths and weaknesses, and could infer their circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Guo had a powerful memory and also possessed stratagem and scheme. He was skilled at observing the enemy's strengths and weaknesses and could infer their circumstances.

sentences.zh: 有潛匿溪穀欲為間偵者，果登高望之，所疑處，往必有獲。

translations.literal: When there were those hiding in streams and valleys wishing to spy, Guo climbed high and looked out; wherever he suspected, if he went there he always made a capture.
translations.idiomatic: When there were those hiding in streams and valleys wishing to spy, Guo climbed high and looked out. Wherever he suspected, he always made a capture.

sentences.zh: 周文由是以果為虞候都督。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou thereupon made Guo Commander of Scouts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou thereupon made Guo Commander of Scouts.

sentences.zh: 每從征行，常領候騎，晝夜巡察，略不眠寢。

translations.literal: On every campaign he regularly commanded scout cavalry, patrolling day and night, scarcely sleeping at all.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign he regularly commanded scout cavalry, patrolling day and night, scarcely sleeping at all.

sentences.zh: 從平竇泰于潼關，周文因其規畫，軍以勝返，賞真珠金帶一條。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Dou Tai at Tong Pass; Emperor Wen of Zhou because of his planning made the army return victorious and rewarded him with one belt of pearl and gold.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in pacifying Dou Tai at Tong Pass. Emperor Wen of Zhou, because of his planning, brought the army back victorious and rewarded him with a belt of pearl and gold.

sentences.zh: 又從復弘農，破沙苑，戰河橋，並有功。

translations.literal: Again he followed in recovering Hongnong, breaking Shaya, and fighting at Heqiao; in each he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed in recovering Hongnong, breaking Shaya, and fighting at Heqiao; in each case he distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 曆朔、安二州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as Regional Inspector of Shuo and An provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Regional Inspector of Shuo and An.

sentences.zh: 從戰芒山，軍還，除河東郡守。

translations.literal: He followed into battle at Mangshan; when the army returned, he was appointed Administrator of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He followed into battle at Mangshan. When the army returned, he was appointed Administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 又從大將軍破稽胡於北山。

translations.literal: Again he followed the Grand General in defeating the Ji Hu at Beishan.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the Grand General in defeating the Ji Hu at Beishan.

sentences.zh: 胡地險阻，人跡罕至，果進兵窮討，散其種落。

translations.literal: The Hu territory was perilous and obstructed, and human tracks rarely reached it; Guo advanced troops in exhaustive pursuit and scattered their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu territory was perilous and obstructed, and human tracks rarely reached it. Guo advanced troops in exhaustive pursuit and scattered their tribes.

sentences.zh: 稽胡憚果勁勇驕捷，號為著翅人。

translations.literal: The Ji Hu feared Guo's fierce bravery and swift agility and called him the Winged Man.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji Hu feared Guo's fierce bravery and swift agility and called him the Winged Man.

sentences.zh: 周文聞之，笑曰：「著翅之名，寧滅飛將。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou heard of it, he said with a laugh: "The name Winged Man—would it not extinguish a flying general?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou heard of it, he said with a laugh, "The name Winged Man—would it not extinguish a flying general?"

sentences.zh: 累遷開府儀同三司、進爵褒中郡公。

translations.literal: By repeated advancement he was transferred to Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and advanced to Duke of Baozhong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: By repeated advancement he was transferred to Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and advanced to Duke of Baozhong.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，拜少師，進位柱國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, he was appointed Junior Mentor and advanced to pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoding, he was appointed Junior Mentor and advanced to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 天和初，授華州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe, he was appointed Regional Inspector of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianhe, he was appointed Regional Inspector of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 為政寬簡，吏人稱之。

translations.literal: His governance was lenient and simple; officials and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was lenient and simple; officials and people praised him.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 梁椿，字千年，代人也。

translations.literal: Liang Chun, courtesy name Qiannian, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chun, styled Qiannian, was from Dai.

sentences.zh: 初從爾硃榮入洛，又從賀拔岳討平万俟醜奴，仍從周文平侯草陳悅。

translations.literal: At first he followed Erzhu Rong into Luoyang, then followed Heba Yue in attacking and pacifying Moqi Chounu, and then followed Emperor Wen of Zhou in pacifying Houcao and Chen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed Erzhu Rong into Luoyang, then Heba Yue in defeating Moqi Chounu, and afterward Emperor Wen of Zhou in pacifying Houcao and Chen Yue.

sentences.zh: 大統中，累以戰功封東平郡公，位開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: During the Datong era, through repeated battle merits he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping Commandery and held Opening Office with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Datong era, repeated battle honors brought him enfeoffment as Duke of Dongping Commandery and the rank Opening Office with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，除華州刺史，改封清陵郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, he was appointed Inspector of Huazhou and his fief was changed to Duke of Qingling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, Chun was appointed Inspector of Huazhou and transferred in fief to Duke of Qingling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，拜大將軍，卒于位。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding, he was appointed Grand General and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 561, he was appointed Grand General and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈都督、恆州刺史，諡曰烈。
