translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of Hengzhou, and his posthumous name was Lie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of Hengzhou, with the posthumous name Lie.

sentences.zh: 椿性果毅，善於撫納，所獲賞物，分賜麾下，故每踐敵場，咸得其死力。

translations.literal: Chun’s nature was resolute and firm, and he was good at comforting and attracting others; the rewards he received he distributed among his subordinates, and so whenever he entered the battlefield, he obtained their desperate effort.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was resolute and firm by nature and good at winning people over. He distributed the rewards he received among his subordinates, so whenever he entered battle, they all fought to the death for him.

sentences.zh: 雅好儉素，不營貲產，時論以此稱焉。

translations.literal: He normally liked frugality and simplicity and did not manage wealth and property; contemporary opinion praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He loved frugality and simplicity and did not seek wealth or property; contemporary opinion praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 子明嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ming succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ming succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 為黎州刺史，與尉遲迥同謀反，被誅。

translations.literal: He was Regional Inspector of Lizhou; he joined Yu Chi Jiong in plotting rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was Regional Inspector of Lizhou. He joined Yuchi Jiong in plotting rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 蔡祐，字承先，其先陳留圉人也。

translations.literal: Cai You, style name Chengxian, his ancestors were men of Yu in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Cai You, courtesy name Chengxian, was descended from men of Yu in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖紹為夏州鎮將，徙居高平，因家焉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shao was garrison general of Xiazhou; he moved to dwell at Gaoping and there established his family.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shao was garrison general of Xiazhou. He moved to Gaoping and there established his family.

sentences.zh: 父襲，名著西州。

translations.literal: His father Xi was famous throughout the western provinces.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xi was famous throughout the western provinces.

sentences.zh: 魏正光中，万俟醜奴亂關中，襲乃背賊歸洛陽。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era of Wei, Moqi Chounu rebelled in Guanzhong; Xi then turned against the rebels and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguang era of Wei, Moqi Chounu rebelled in Guanzhong. Xi then turned against the rebels and returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 拜齊安郡守。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Qi'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Qi'an.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，始拔難西歸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, he at last escaped hardship and returned west.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, he at last escaped hardship and returned west.

sentences.zh: 賜爵平舒縣伯，除岐、雍二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Count of Pingshu county and appointed Regional Inspector of Qi and Yong provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the title Count of Pingshu and appointed Regional Inspector of Qi and Yong.

sentences.zh: 祐性聰敏，有行檢。

translations.literal: You's nature was clever and keen; he had moral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: You was clever and keen by nature and possessed moral integrity.

sentences.zh: 襲之背賊東歸，祐年十四，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: When Xi turned against the rebels and returned east, You was fourteen years old and was known for serving his mother with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi turned against the rebels and returned east, You was fourteen years old and was known for serving his mother with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 及長，有膂力。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he had physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he had great physical strength.

sentences.zh: 周文在原州，召為帳下親信。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou was at Yuanzhou, he summoned You as a trusted attendant in his tent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou was at Yuanzhou, he summoned You as a trusted attendant in his tent.

sentences.zh: 及遷夏州，以祐為都督。

translations.literal: When he moved to Xiazhou, he made You commander.
translations.idiomatic: When he moved to Xiazhou, he made You commander.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳悅害賀拔岳，諸將迎周文，周文將赴之。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue killed Heba Yue; the generals welcomed Emperor Wen of Zhou, and Emperor Wen was about to go to them.
translations.idiomatic: When Houmochen Yue killed Heba Yue, the generals welcomed Emperor Wen of Zhou, and Emperor Wen was about to go to them.

sentences.zh: 夏州首望彌姐元進等陰有異計。

translations.literal: The leading figures of Xiazhou, Mijie Yuanjin and others, secretly had a different plan.
translations.idiomatic: The leading figures of Xiazhou, Mijie Yuanjin and others, secretly harbored a different plan.

sentences.zh: 周文微知之，召元進等入計事，既而目祐。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou faintly knew of it; he summoned Yuanjin and others to enter and discuss affairs, then glanced at You.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou faintly knew of it. He summoned Yuanjin and others to discuss affairs, then glanced at You.

sentences.zh: 祐即出外，衣甲持刀直入，叱元進而斬之，並其黨伏誅。

translations.literal: You immediately went outside, donned armor, took a blade, and entered directly; he shouted at Yuanjin and beheaded him, and together with his faction they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: You immediately went outside, donned armor, took a blade, and entered directly. He shouted at Yuanjin and beheaded him, and his faction was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 一坐皆戰慄。

translations.literal: All those seated trembled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: All those seated trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 於是與諸將盟，同心誅悅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he allied with the generals in oath, of one mind to execute Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he allied with the generals in oath, united in mind to execute Yue.

sentences.zh: 周文以此重之，謂祐曰：「吾今以爾為子，爾其父事我。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou because of this valued him highly and said to You: "I now take you as my son; you should serve me as a father."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou because of this valued him highly and said to You, "I now take you as my son; you should serve me as a father."

sentences.zh: 栗迎孝武於潼關，以前後功封萇鄉縣伯。

translations.literal: He then welcomed Emperor Xiaowu at Tong Pass and for his earlier and later merit was enfeoffed as Count of Changxiang county.
translations.idiomatic: He then welcomed Emperor Xiaowu at Tong Pass and for his earlier and later merit was enfeoffed as Count of Changxiang.

sentences.zh: 後從禽竇泰，復弘農，戰沙苑，皆有功。

translations.literal: Later he followed in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and fighting at Shaya; in each he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and fighting at Shaya; in each case he distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 授平東將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Palace Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Palace Affairs.

sentences.zh: 又從戰河橋，祐下馬步鬥，左右勸乘馬以備急卒。

translations.literal: Again he followed into battle at Heqiao; You dismounted and fought on foot; those beside him urged him to mount a horse against sudden attack.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed into battle at Heqiao. You dismounted and fought on foot; those beside him urged him to mount a horse against sudden attack.

sentences.zh: 祐怒之曰：「丞相養我如子，今日豈以性命為念？」

translations.literal: You angrily said: "The Chancellor raised me like a son—today how could I be concerned for my life?"
translations.idiomatic: You angrily said, "The Chancellor raised me like a son—today how could I be concerned for my life?"

sentences.zh: 遂率左右十餘人，齊聲大呼，殺傷甚多。

translations.literal: He then led more than ten men beside him, all shouting together in one voice, and killed and wounded many.
translations.idiomatic: He then led more than ten men beside him, all shouting together, and killed and wounded many.

sentences.zh: 敵以其無繼，圍之十餘重。

translations.literal: The enemy because he had no reinforcements surrounded him more than ten layers deep.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy, seeing he had no reinforcements, surrounded him more than ten layers deep.

sentences.zh: 祐乃彎弓持滿，四面拒之。

translations.literal: You then bent his bow to the full and resisted on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: You then bent his bow to the full and resisted on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 東魏人乃募厚甲長刀者，直進取祐。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei men then recruited men in heavy armor with long blades to advance straight and seize You.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Wei men then recruited men in heavy armor with long blades to advance straight at You.

sentences.zh: 去祐可三十步，左右勸射之。

translations.literal: When they were about thirty paces from You, those beside him urged him to shoot.
translations.idiomatic: When they were about thirty paces from You, those beside him urged him to shoot.

sentences.zh: 祐曰：「吾曹性命，在此一矢耳，豈虛發哉！」

translations.literal: You said: "Our lives hang on this one arrow—how could I release it in vain!"
translations.idiomatic: You said, "Our lives hang on this one arrow—how could I release it in vain!"

sentences.zh: 敵人可十步，祐乃射之，中其面，應弦而倒，便以槊刺殺之。

translations.literal: When the enemy was about ten paces away, You then shot; he hit the man's face and he fell at the twang of the string; You then stabbed and killed him with a spear.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy was about ten paces away, You shot. He hit the man's face and the man fell at the twang of the string; You then stabbed and killed him with a spear.

sentences.zh: 敵乃稍卻。

translations.literal: The enemy then slightly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then slightly withdrew.

sentences.zh: 祐乃徐引退。

translations.literal: You then slowly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: You then slowly withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是戰也，西軍不利，周文已還。

translations.literal: In this battle the western army was at a disadvantage; Emperor Wen of Zhou had already returned.
translations.idiomatic: In this battle the western army was at a disadvantage; Emperor Wen of Zhou had already returned.

sentences.zh: 祐至弘農，夜與周文會。

translations.literal: You reached Hongnong and at night met with Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: You reached Hongnong and met with Emperor Wen of Zhou that night.

sentences.zh: 周文字之曰：「承先，爾來吾無憂矣！」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou addressed him saying: "Chengxian, since you have come I have no worries!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou addressed him, saying, "Chengxian, since you have come I have no worries!"

sentences.zh: 周文驚，不得寢，枕祐股上乃安。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou was startled and could not sleep; only when he rested his head on You's thigh did he settle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou was startled and could not sleep; only when he rested his head on You's thigh did he settle.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵為公，授京兆郡守。

translations.literal: For merit his rank was advanced to duke and he was appointed Administrator of Jingzhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For merit his rank was advanced to duke and he was appointed Administrator of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 高仲密舉北豫來附，周文率軍援之，與齊神武遇於芒山。

translations.literal: Gao Zhongmi raised Beiyu and came over; Emperor Wen of Zhou led an army to aid him and encountered Qi Shenwu at Mangshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi raised Beiyu and defected, Emperor Wen of Zhou led an army to aid him and encountered Gao Huan at Mangshan.

sentences.zh: 祐時著明光鐵鎧，所向無敵。

translations.literal: You at the time wore bright iron armor and was invincible wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: You at the time wore bright iron armor and was invincible wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 齊人咸曰：「此是鐵猛獸也。」

translations.literal: The Qi men all said: "This is an iron fierce beast."
translations.idiomatic: The Qi men all said, "This is an iron fierce beast."

sentences.zh: 皆避之。

translations.literal: They all avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: They all avoided him.

sentences.zh: 曆青、原二州刺史，尋除大都督。

translations.literal: He served as Regional Inspector of Qing and Yuan provinces; soon he was appointed Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Regional Inspector of Qing and Yuan; soon he was appointed Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂，請終喪紀，弗許。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his father and requested to complete the mourning period; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he requested to complete the mourning period; it was not granted.

sentences.zh: 累遷開府儀同三司，加侍中，賜姓大利稽氏，進爵懷寧郡公。

translations.literal: By repeated advancement he was transferred to Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, given the additional title Palace Attendant, granted the surname Daliqi, and advanced to Duke of Huaining commandery.
translations.idiomatic: By repeated advancement he was transferred to Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, given the additional title Palace Attendant, granted the surname Daliqi, and advanced to Duke of Huaining.

sentences.zh: 六官建，授兵部中大夫。

translations.literal: When the six offices were established, he was appointed Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When the six offices were established, he was appointed Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 周文不豫，祐與晉公護、賀蘭祥等侍疾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou was unwell, You together with Duke of Jin Hu, Helan Xiang, and others attended his illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou was unwell, You together with Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, Helan Xiang, and others attended his illness.

sentences.zh: 及周文崩，祐悲慕不已，遂得氣疾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou died, You grieved and longed for him without cease and consequently contracted a qi illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou died, You grieved for him without cease and consequently contracted a respiratory illness.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，拜少保。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, You was appointed Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, You was appointed Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 祐與尉遲綱俱掌禁兵。

translations.literal: You and Yuchi Gang together commanded the palace troops.
translations.idiomatic: You and Yuchi Gang jointly commanded the palace troops.

sentences.zh: 時帝信任司會李植等，謀害晉公護。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor trusted Li Zhi, Director of Accounts, and others, and plotted to harm Hu, Duke of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor trusted Li Zhi, Director of Accounts, and others, and plotted against Yuwen Hu, Duke of Jin.

sentences.zh: 祐每泣諫，帝不聽。

translations.literal: You repeatedly remonstrated in tears, but the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: You repeatedly remonstrated with tears, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 尋而帝廢。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the emperor was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, the emperor was deposed.

sentences.zh: 明帝之為公子也，與祐特相友昵，及即位，禮遇彌隆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was still a prince, he was especially friendly and intimate with You; when he ascended the throne, his courteous treatment became still more exalted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming was still a prince, he was especially close to You, and after taking the throne, treated him with even greater honor.

sentences.zh: 加拜小司馬。

translations.literal: You was additionally appointed Junior Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: You was additionally appointed Junior Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 禦膳每有異味，輒以賜祐，群臣朝宴，每被別留，或至昏夜，列炬鳴笳，送祐還宅。

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial meals had unusual flavors, they were bestowed on You; at court banquets with the ministers, he was always kept behind separately, sometimes until dusk or night, and torches were arrayed and reed pipes sounded to escort You back to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the imperial kitchen had some unusual delicacy, it was bestowed on You. At court banquets, he was often kept behind after the other ministers, sometimes until nightfall, and was escorted home with torches arrayed and pipes sounding.

sentences.zh: 祐以過蒙殊遇，常辭疾避之。

translations.literal: Because You received extraordinary treatment beyond measure, he often declined on grounds of illness to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Because You felt this exceptional favor was excessive, he often pleaded illness to avoid it.

sentences.zh: 至於婚姻，尤不願結于權要。

translations.literal: As for marriage alliances, he was especially unwilling to form them with the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: As for marriage alliances, he was especially unwilling to connect himself with the powerful.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官權鎮原州。

translations.literal: Soon, retaining his original office, he temporarily guarded Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, while retaining his office, he was temporarily assigned to guard Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，授宜州刺史。

translations.literal: After a short time, he was appointed Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he was appointed Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 未之部，卒于原州。

translations.literal: Before going to his jurisdiction, he died in Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached his post, he died in Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 祐少與鄉人李穆布衣齊名，常相謂曰：「大丈夫當建立功名，以取富貴，安能久處貧賤。」

translations.literal: In youth You was equally famous as a commoner with his fellow townsman Li Mu; they often said to each other: "A great man should establish merit and fame to obtain wealth and rank—how can he long remain in poverty and low status?"
translations.idiomatic: In youth You was equally famous as a commoner with his fellow townsman Li Mu. They often said to each other, "A great man should establish merit and fame to obtain wealth and rank—how can he long remain in poverty and low status?"

sentences.zh: 言訖，各大笑。

translations.literal: When the words were finished, each laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: When the words were finished, each laughed loudly.

sentences.zh: 後皆如言。

translations.literal: Later both were as they had said.
translations.idiomatic: Later both fulfilled their words.

sentences.zh: 及從征伐，為士卒先。

translations.literal: When he followed on campaigns, he was ahead of the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed on campaigns, he led from the front.

sentences.zh: 軍還，諸將爭功，祐終無所競。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the generals competed for credit; You in the end never contended.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, the generals competed for credit; You never contended.

sentences.zh: 周文每歎之曰：「承先口不言勳，孤當代其論敘。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou often sighed and said: "Chengxian never speaks of merit—I must narrate it in his place."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou often sighed and said, "Chengxian never speaks of merit—I must narrate it in his place."

sentences.zh: 性節儉，所得祿秩，皆散宗族，身死之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: His nature was frugal; the salary and rank he received he distributed among his clan; on the day he died his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He was frugal by nature. The salary and rank he received he distributed among his clan, and on the day he died his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 贈柱國大將軍、原州都督，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Pillar of State Grand General and Commander of Yuanzhou, with posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Pillar of State Grand General and Commander of Yuanzhou, with the posthumous title Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子正嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 祐弟澤，頗好學，有幹能。

translations.literal: You's younger brother Ze was quite fond of learning and had practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: You's younger brother Ze was quite fond of learning and possessed practical ability.

sentences.zh: 後為𨝽州刺史，以不從司馬消難被害。

translations.literal: Later he was Regional Inspector of Yunzhou and was killed for not following Sima Xiaonan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Regional Inspector of Yunzhou and was killed for refusing to follow Sima Xiaonan.

sentences.zh: 常善，高陽人也。

translations.literal: Chang Shan was a man of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shan was a native of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 家本豪族。

translations.literal: His family was originally a powerful clan.
translations.idiomatic: His family was originally a powerful clan.

sentences.zh: 魏孝昌中，從爾硃榮入洛，封房城縣男。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era of Wei, he followed Erzhu Rong into Luoyang and was enfeoffed as Baron of Fangcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era of Wei, he followed Erzhu Rong into Luoyang and was enfeoffed as Baron of Fangcheng.

sentences.zh: 後周文平侯莫陳悅，除天水郡守。

translations.literal: Later when Emperor Wen of Zhou pacified Houmochen Yue, he was appointed Administrator of Tianshui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Emperor Wen of Zhou pacified Houmochen Yue, he was appointed Administrator of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 累遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、西安州刺史，轉蔚州刺史。

translations.literal: By repeated advancement he was transferred to Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, and Regional Inspector of Xi'anzhou, then transferred to Regional Inspector of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: By repeated advancement he was transferred to Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, and Regional Inspector of Xi'anzhou, then to Regional Inspector of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 頻蒞二籓，有政績。

translations.literal: He repeatedly held two frontier posts and had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly held two frontier posts and achieved distinction in governance.

sentences.zh: 進爵永陽郡公。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to Duke of Yongyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was advanced to Duke of Yongyang.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，拜大將軍、甯州總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou acceded to the throne, he was appointed Grand General and Grand Governor of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou acceded to the throne, he was appointed Grand General and Grand Governor of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，入為小司徒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, he entered the capital as Junior Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding, he entered the capital as Junior Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈柱國大將軍、都督、延州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Pillar of State Grand General, Commander, and Regional Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Pillar of State Grand General, Commander, and Regional Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 子昂和嗣。

translations.literal: His son Anghe succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anghe succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 辛威，隴西人也。

translations.literal: Xin Wei was a man of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Wei was a native of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 少慷慨有志略。

translations.literal: In youth he was magnanimous and had ambition and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was magnanimous and possessed ambition and strategy.

sentences.zh: 初從賀拔岳征伐有功，假輔國將軍、都督。

translations.literal: At first he followed Heba Yue on campaigns with merit and was provisionally appointed General Who Supports the State and commander.
translations.idiomatic: At first he followed Heba Yue on campaigns with distinction and was provisionally appointed General Who Supports the State and commander.

sentences.zh: 及周文統嶽眾，見威奇之，引為帳內，封白土縣伯，後進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou took command of Yue's forces, he saw Wei was extraordinary and brought him into the tent guard; he was enfeoffed as Count of Baitu county and later advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou took command of Yue's forces, he saw Wei was extraordinary and brought him into the tent guard. He was enfeoffed as Count of Baitu and later advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 累遷開府儀同三司，賜姓普屯氏。

translations.literal: By repeated advancement he was transferred to Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and granted the surname Putun.
translations.idiomatic: By repeated advancement he was transferred to Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and granted the surname Putun.

sentences.zh: 出為鄜州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Regional Inspector of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Regional Inspector of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 威時望既重，朝廷以桑梓榮之，遷河州刺史、本州大中正。

translations.literal: Because Wei's contemporary renown was already weighty, the court honored him in his native place and transferred him to Regional Inspector of Hezhou and Grand Rectifier of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wei's contemporary renown was already great, the court honored him in his native place and transferred him to Regional Inspector of Hezhou and Grand Rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 頻領二鎮，頗得人和。

translations.literal: He repeatedly held two garrison posts and quite won the harmony of the people.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly held two garrison posts and won the harmony of the people.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，拜大將軍，進爵枹罕郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou acceded to the throne, he was appointed Grand General and advanced to Duke of Fuhan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou acceded to the throne, he was appointed Grand General and advanced to Duke of Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，進位上柱國。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng, he was advanced to Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng, he was advanced to Senior Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 大象二年，進封宿國公，復為少傅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daxiang, he was advanced to Duke of Su and again appointed Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daxiang, he was advanced to Duke of Su and again appointed Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 威性持重，有威嚴。

translations.literal: Wei's nature was steady and weighty; he had imposing dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was steady and weighty by nature and possessed imposing dignity.

sentences.zh: 曆官數十年，未嘗有過，故得以身名終。

translations.literal: He held office for several decades and never had an offense; therefore he was able to finish with body and name intact.
translations.idiomatic: He held office for several decades without ever committing an offense; therefore he was able to finish his career with reputation intact.

sentences.zh: 兼其家有義，五世同居，時以此稱之。

translations.literal: Moreover his family had righteousness; five generations lived together, and at the time he was praised for this.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his family was known for righteousness; five generations lived together, and at the time he was praised for this.

sentences.zh: 子永達嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yongda succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongda succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 位儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: His post was General with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of General with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 厙狄昌，字恃德，神武人也。

translations.literal: She Dichang, style name Shide, was a man of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: She Dichang, courtesy name Shide, was a native of Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 少便弓馬，有膂力。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled with bow and horse and had physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was skilled with bow and horse and had great physical strength.

sentences.zh: 及長，進止閒雅，膽氣壯烈，每以將帥自許。

translations.literal: When he grew up, his bearing was leisurely and refined, his courage and spirit fierce and resolute; he always considered himself fit to be a general.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, his bearing was leisurely and refined, his courage and spirit fierce and resolute. He always considered himself fit to be a general.

sentences.zh: 從爾硃天光定關中。

translations.literal: He followed Erzhu Tianguang in pacifying Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Erzhu Tianguang in pacifying Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 天光敗，又從賀拔嶽征討。

translations.literal: When Tianguang was defeated, he again followed Heba Yue on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang was defeated, he again followed Heba Yue on campaigns.

sentences.zh: 及岳被害，昌與諸將議翊戴周文。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed, Chang together with the generals deliberated on supporting and installing Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was killed, Chang and the other generals deliberated on supporting and installing Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 從平侯莫陳悅，賜爵陰盤縣子。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Houmochen Yue and was granted the title Viscount of Yinpan county.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in pacifying Houmochen Yue and was granted the title Viscount of Yinpan.

sentences.zh: 後從迎孝武，復潼關，改封長子縣子。

translations.literal: Later he followed in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu and recovering Tong Pass; his enfeoffment was changed to Viscount of Changzi county.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu and recovering Tong Pass, and his enfeoffment was changed to Viscount of Changzi.

sentences.zh: 大統初，累遷開府儀同三司，進爵方城公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, by repeated advancement he was transferred to Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and advanced to Duke of Fangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Datong, by repeated advancement he was transferred to Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and advanced to Duke of Fangcheng.

sentences.zh: 六官建，授稍伯中大夫。

translations.literal: When the six offices were established, he was appointed Director in the Ministry of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When the six offices were established, he was appointed Director in the Ministry of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou acceded to the throne, he was appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou acceded to the throne, he was appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子明，以椿功賜爵豐陽縣公。

translations.literal: His son Ming, because of Chun's merit, was granted the title Duke of Fengyang county.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ming, because of Chun's merit, was granted the title Duke of Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 後襲椿爵，舊封回授弟朗。

translations.literal: Later he inherited Chun's title and returned the old enfeoffment to his younger brother Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he inherited Chun's title and returned the old enfeoffment to his younger brother Lang.

sentences.zh: 梁台，字洛都，萇池人也。

translations.literal: Liang Tai, style name Luodu, was a man of Changchi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Tai, courtesy name Luodu, was a native of Changchi.

sentences.zh: 少果敢，有志操。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and resolute and had moral integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was bold and resolute and possessed moral integrity.

sentences.zh: 從爾硃天光平關、隴，賜爵隴城鄉男。

translations.literal: He followed Erzhu Tianguang in pacifying Guan and Long and was granted the title Baron of Longcheng township.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Erzhu Tianguang in pacifying Guan and Long and was granted the title Baron of Longcheng township.

sentences.zh: 及天光敗于韓陵，賀拔嶽又引為心膂。

translations.literal: When Tianguang was defeated at Hanling, Heba Yue again brought him in as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang was defeated at Hanling, Heba Yue again brought him in as a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 岳為侯莫陳悅所害，台與諸將翊戴周文。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, Tai together with the generals supported and installed Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, Tai and the other generals supported and installed Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 從平悅，累功授潁州刺史，賜姓賀蘭氏。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Yue; by accumulated merit he was appointed Regional Inspector of Yingzhou and granted the surname Helan.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in pacifying Yue. By accumulated merit he was appointed Regional Inspector of Yingzhou and granted the surname Helan.

sentences.zh: 累遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同、侍中。

translations.literal: By repeated advancement he was transferred to Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: By repeated advancement he was transferred to Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，進爵中部縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou acceded to the throne, his rank was advanced to Duke of Zhongbu county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou acceded to the throne, his rank was advanced to Duke of Zhongbu.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, he was appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Baoding, he was appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 時大軍圍洛陽，久不拔。

translations.literal: At the time the great army besieged Luoyang but for a long time could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the main army besieged Luoyang but for a long time could not take it.

sentences.zh: 齊騎奄至，齊公憲禦之。

translations.literal: Qi cavalry suddenly arrived; Duke of Qi Xian resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: Qi cavalry suddenly arrived; Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian resisted them.

sentences.zh: 有數人為敵所執，已去。

translations.literal: Several men were seized by the enemy and had already been taken away.
translations.idiomatic: Several men were seized by the enemy and had already been taken away.

sentences.zh: 台單馬突入，射殺兩人，敵皆披靡，被執者遂還。

translations.literal: Tai alone on horseback charged in, shot and killed two men, the enemy all were routed, and those seized were thus recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Tai alone on horseback charged in, shot and killed two men, routed the enemy, and recovered those who had been seized.

sentences.zh: 齊公憲每歎曰：「梁台果毅膽決，不可及也。」

translations.literal: Duke of Qi Xian often sighed and said: "Liang Tai is resolute, bold, and decisive—he cannot be matched."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian often sighed and said, "Liang Tai is resolute, bold, and decisive—he cannot be matched."

sentences.zh: 五年，拜鄜州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Regional Inspector of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Regional Inspector of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 台性疏通，恕以待物，至於蒞人，尤以惠愛為心。

translations.literal: Tai's nature was open and penetrating; he treated things with forbearance, and in governing people he especially took benevolence and kindness to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was open and penetrating by nature and treated others with forbearance. In governing people he especially took benevolence and kindness to heart.

sentences.zh: 不過識千餘字，口占書啟，詞意可觀。

translations.literal: He knew no more than a thousand characters; he dictated letters and memorials orally, and their wording and meaning were respectable.
translations.idiomatic: He knew no more than a thousand characters, yet he dictated letters and memorials orally with respectable wording and meaning.

sentences.zh: 年過六十，猶能被甲跨馬，足不躡鐙，馳射弋獵，矢不虛發。

translations.literal: Past sixty years of age, he could still don armor and mount a horse without treading the stirrups, gallop and shoot, hunt with bow, and never release an arrow in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Past sixty years of age, he could still don armor and mount a horse without treading the stirrups, gallop and shoot, hunt with bow, and never release an arrow in vain.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 田弘，字廣略，高平人也。

translations.literal: Tian Hong, style name Guanglue, was a man of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hong, courtesy name Guanglue, was a native of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 少慷慨，有謀略。

translations.literal: In youth he was magnanimous and had strategy.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was magnanimous and possessed strategy.

sentences.zh: 初陷万俟醜奴。

translations.literal: At first he was captured by Moqi Chounu.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was captured by Moqi Chounu.

sentences.zh: 爾硃天光入關，弘自原州歸順。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Tianguang entered the Pass, Hong from Yuanzhou submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tianguang entered the Pass, Hong submitted from Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 及周文統眾，弘求謁見，乃論時事，即處以爪牙之任。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou took command of the forces, Hong requested an audience; he then discussed current affairs and was immediately placed in a role as claw and fang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou took command of the forces, Hong requested an audience, discussed current affairs, and was immediately placed in a trusted military role.

sentences.zh: 又以迎孝武功，封鶉陰縣子。

translations.literal: Again for merit in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Chunyin county.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Chunyin.

sentences.zh: 周文嘗以所著鐵甲賜弘，云：「天下若定，還將此甲示孤也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou once bestowed on Hong the iron armor he himself had worn, saying: "If the realm is pacified, bring this armor back to show me."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou once bestowed on Hong the iron armor he himself had worn, saying, "If the realm is pacified, bring this armor back to show me."

sentences.zh: 累功賜姓紇幹氏，授原州刺史。

translations.literal: By accumulated merit he was granted the surname Hegan and appointed Regional Inspector of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By accumulated merit he was granted the surname Hegan and appointed Regional Inspector of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 以弘勳望兼至，故以衣錦榮之。

translations.literal: Because Hong's merit and renown were both complete, he was thus honored with return in glory to his home.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hong's merit and renown were both complete, he was honored with return in glory to his home.

sentences.zh: 周文在同州，文武並集，乃謂之曰：「人人如弘盡心，天下豈不早定？」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou was at Tongzhou, civil and military officials all gathered; he then said to them: "If every man were as devoted as Hong, would the realm not have been pacified long ago?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou was at Tongzhou, civil and military officials all gathered. He then said to them, "If every man were as devoted as Hong, would the realm not have been pacified long ago?"

sentences.zh: 即授車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei, he was given the additional titles Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei, he was given the additional titles Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening-general with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 平蜀後，梁信州刺史蕭韶等未從朝化，詔弘討平之。

translations.literal: After the pacification of Shu, Xiao Shao of Liang, Regional Inspector of Xinzhou, and others had not yet submitted to court transformation; an edict ordered Hong to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Shu, Xiao Shao of Liang, Regional Inspector of Xinzhou, and others had not yet submitted to the court. An edict ordered Hong to campaign and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 又討西平反羌及鳳州叛氐等，並破之。

translations.literal: Again he campaigned against the Fan Qiang of Xiping and the rebel Di of Fengzhou and others, and in each case broke them.
translations.idiomatic: He also campaigned against the Fan Qiang of Xiping and the rebel Di of Fengzhou and others, defeating them all.

sentences.zh: 每臨陣，推鋒直前，身被一百餘箭，破骨者九，馬被十槊。

translations.literal: Whenever he faced battle, he pushed the vanguard straight forward; his body was struck by more than a hundred arrows, nine pierced to the bone, and his horse was struck by ten spears.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he faced battle, he pushed the vanguard straight forward. His body was struck by more than a hundred arrows, nine pierced to the bone, and his horse was struck by ten spears.

sentences.zh: 朝廷壯之。

translations.literal: The court admired him.
translations.idiomatic: The court admired him.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔踐阼，進爵雁門郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou acceded to the throne, his rank was advanced to Duke of Yanmen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou acceded to the throne, his rank was advanced to Duke of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，出為岷州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding, he went out as Regional Inspector of Minzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoding, he went out as Regional Inspector of Minzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘雖武將，而動遵法式，百姓賴安之。

translations.literal: Although Hong was a military general, in action he observed law and regulation; the common people relied on him and were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Although Hong was a military general, in action he observed law and regulation, and the common people relied on him and lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 三年，從隨公楊忠伐齊，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Duke of Sui Yang Zhong in campaigning against Qi and was appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed Duke of Sui Yang Zhong in campaigning against Qi and was appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 後進柱國大將軍，歷位大司空、少保、襄州總管。

translations.literal: Later he was advanced to Pillar of State Grand General and successively held the posts of Grand Minister of Works, Junior Mentor, and Grand Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was advanced to Pillar of State Grand General and successively held the posts of Grand Minister of Works, Junior Mentor, and Grand Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 薨於州。

translations.literal: He died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子仁恭嗣。

translations.literal: His son Rengong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rengong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 仁恭，字長貴。

translations.literal: Rengong, style name Changgui.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong, courtesy name Changgui.

sentences.zh: 性寬仁，有局度。

translations.literal: His nature was generous and benevolent; he had breadth of vision.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous and benevolent by nature and possessed breadth of vision.

sentences.zh: 歷位幽州總管。

translations.literal: He successively held the post of Grand Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of Grand Governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，進上柱國，拜太子太師，甚見親重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was advanced to Senior Pillar of State and appointed Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince; he was greatly trusted and honored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was advanced to Senior Pillar of State and appointed Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince. He was greatly trusted and honored.

sentences.zh: 嘗幸其第，宴飲極歡，禮賜甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor once visited his residence; the banquet and drinking were extremely joyous, and ceremonial gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once visited his residence. The banquet was extremely joyous, and the ceremonial gifts were very generous.

sentences.zh: 尋奉詔營太廟，進爵觀國公，拜右武衛大將軍，轉左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he received an edict to construct the Imperial Ancestral Temple; his rank was advanced to Duke of Guan; he was appointed Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and transferred to Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received an edict to construct the Imperial Ancestral Temple. His rank was advanced to Duke of Guan, he was appointed Grand General of the Right Martial Guard, and was transferred to Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈司空，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died in office and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works with posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 子世師嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shishi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shishi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 次子德懋，少以孝友知名。

translations.literal: His second son Demao in youth was known for filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Demao was known from youth for filial piety and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，以父軍功賜爵平原郡公，授太子千牛備身。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, because of his father's military merit he was granted the title Duke of Pingyuan commandery and appointed Attendant of the Crown Prince's Thousand Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang, because of his father's military merit he was granted the title Duke of Pingyuan and appointed Attendant of the Crown Prince's Thousand Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 丁父艱，哀毀骨立，廬於墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: When his father died he mourned until he was wasted to the bone; he built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to form the grave mound.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he mourned until he was wasted to the bone. He built a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to form the grave mound.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而嘉之，遣員外散騎侍郎元志就吊焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he commended him and dispatched Attendant Cavalier Yuan Zhi to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he commended him and dispatched Attendant Cavalier Yuan Zhi to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 復降璽書存問，賜帛及米，下詔表其閭。

translations.literal: Again an imperial letter was sent to inquire after him; silk and rice were bestowed, and an edict was issued to honor his village.
translations.idiomatic: Again an imperial letter was sent to inquire after him. Silk and rice were bestowed, and an edict was issued to honor his village.

sentences.zh: 大業中，位尚書駕部郎，卒官。

translations.literal: In the Daye era his post was Director in the Ministry of Works' Chariot Section; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era he held the post of Director in the Ministry of Works' Chariot Section and died in office.

sentences.zh: 時有玉城郡公王景、鮮虞縣公謝慶恩並位上柱國；

translations.literal: At the time Duke of Yucheng Wang Jing and Duke of Xianyu Xie Qing'en both held the post of Senior Pillar of State;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Duke of Yucheng Wang Jing and Duke of Xianyu Xie Qing'en both held the post of Senior Pillar of State;

sentences.zh: 大義公辛遵及其弟韶並位柱國。

translations.literal: Duke of Dayi Xin Zun and his younger brother Shao both held the post of Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Dayi Xin Zun and his younger brother Shao both held the post of Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝以其俱佐命功臣，特加崇貴，親禮與仁恭等，事皆亡失云。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui because they were all founding-assistance merit officials specially added honor and esteem and personally treated them with ceremony equal to Rengong and others; their affairs are all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui, because they were all founding-assistance merit officials, specially added honor and esteem and personally treated them with ceremony equal to Rengong and others; their records are all lost.

sentences.zh: 論曰：周文接喪亂之際，乘戰爭之餘，發跡平涼，撫征關右。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Emperor Wen of Zhou received the age of mourning and chaos, rode the aftermath of war, rose from Pingliang, and pacified and campaigned in Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Emperor Wen of Zhou came to power amid mourning and chaos, in the aftermath of war. He rose from Pingliang and pacified and campaigned in Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 于時外虞孔熾，內難方殷，羽檄交馳，戎軒屢駕，終能蕩清逋孽，克固鴻基。

translations.literal: At the time external alarms were intensely blazing and internal troubles were just severe; military dispatches crossed in flight and the war chariot was repeatedly driven forth; in the end he was able to sweep clear fleeing rebels and firmly consolidate the great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: At the time external alarms blazed and internal troubles were severe. Military dispatches flew back and forth and the war chariot was repeatedly driven forth. In the end he was able to sweep clear fleeing rebels and firmly consolidate the great foundation.

sentences.zh: 雖稟算於廟堂，實責成於將帥。

translations.literal: Although plans were received in the temple hall, in reality completion was entrusted to the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Although plans were made in the temple hall, in reality completion depended on the generals.

sentences.zh: 達奚武、若干惠、怡峰、劉亮、王德、赫連達、韓果、蔡祐、常善、辛威、厙狄昌、梁椿、梁台、田弘等，並兼資勇略，咸會風雲，或效績中權，或立功方面，均分休戚，同濟艱危，可謂國之爪牙，朝之禦侮者也。

translations.literal: Da Xiwu, Ruo Ganhui, Yi Feng, Liu Liang, Wang De, He Lianda, Han Guo, Cai You, Chang Shan, Xin Wei, She Dichang, Liang Chun, Liang Tai, Tian Hong, and others all combined courage and strategy, all met the moment of opportunity; some achieved merit at the center of power, some established merit on the frontiers; they equally shared joy and sorrow and together crossed through hardship and peril—they can be called the claws and fangs of the state and the defenders against insult for the court.
translations.idiomatic: Da Xiwu, Ruo Ganhui, Yi Feng, Liu Liang, Wang De, He Lianda, Han Guo, Cai You, Chang Shan, Xin Wei, She Dichang, Liang Chun, Liang Tai, Tian Hong, and others all combined courage and strategy and met the moment of opportunity. Some achieved merit at the center of power, some established merit on the frontiers. They equally shared joy and sorrow and together crossed through hardship and peril—they can be called the claws and fangs of the state and the defenders against insult for the court.

sentences.zh: 而武協規文後，得雋小關，周瑜赤壁之謀，賈詡烏巢之策，何以能尚？

translations.literal: Yet Wu coordinated plans after Emperor Wen and achieved brilliance at Xiaoguan—how could the stratagem of Zhou Yu at Red Cliff or the plan of Jia Xu at Wuchao compare?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wu coordinated plans after Emperor Wen and achieved brilliance at Xiaoguan—how could the stratagem of Zhou Yu at Red Cliff or the plan of Jia Xu at Wuchao compare?

sentences.zh: 一言興邦，斯之謂矣。

translations.literal: One word raises the state—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: One word raises the state—this is what is meant.

sentences.zh: 惠、德本以果毅知名，而能率由孝道，雖圖史所歎，何以加焉？

translations.literal: Hui and De were originally known for resolute boldness, yet were able to follow filial piety—though histories sigh in admiration, how could one add to this?
translations.idiomatic: Hui and De were originally known for resolute boldness, yet were able to follow filial piety. Though histories sigh in admiration, how could one add to this?

sentences.zh: 勇者不必有仁，斯不然矣。

translations.literal: The brave need not have benevolence—this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: The brave need not have benevolence—this is not so.

sentences.zh: 以赫連達之先識而加之以仁恕，蔡祐之敢勇而終之以不伐，斯豈企及之所致乎，抑亦天性而已。

translations.literal: That He Lianda had foresight and added to it benevolence and forbearance, and that Cai You had daring courage and ended with not boasting of merit—is this something attained by striving, or simply innate nature?
translations.idiomatic: That He Lianda had foresight and added to it benevolence and forbearance, and that Cai You had daring courage yet did not boast of merit—is this something attained by striving, or simply innate nature?

sentences.zh: 仁恭出內榮顯，豈徒然哉。

translations.literal: Rengong's rise from the interior to glory and prominence—was it for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: Rengong's rise from the interior to glory and prominence—was it for nothing?

sentences.zh: 德懋道協天經，亦足嘉矣。

translations.literal: Demao's way accorded with Heaven's constant—this too is worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Demao's way accorded with Heaven's constant—this too is worthy of praise.
